name: Aloo bhate bhat
instructions: Wash the basmati rice in clean water until the water runs clear; drain.
Peel the raw potato and keep it whole so it cooks alongside the rice without disintegrating.
In a deep pot, combine the drained rice, the whole potato and about three cups of water.
Place over medium-high heat and bring to a boil; then lower the heat, cover, and cook for fifteen minutes until rice is done and potato is fork-tender.
Scoop the boiled potato out of the rice and transfer to a mixing bowl.
Add the chopped onion, chopped green chilli, salt and raw mustard oil to the hot potato.
Mash everything together with a spoon until smooth and well combined.
Serve the spiced potato mash alongside steaming portions of the boiled rice.

name: Aloo Gobi
instructions: Heat mustard oil in a heavy pan until it smokes slightly, then reduce heat.
Add the potato cubes and shallow fry them until they are lightly golden. Remove and set aside.
In the same oil, fry the cauliflower florets until they develop a slight brown crust. Remove and set aside.
If needed, add a little more oil. Add cumin seeds, ginger, and green chilli, and sauté for a few seconds.
Lower the heat and add turmeric powder, red chilli powder, and coriander powder. Quickly stir to prevent burning.
Return the fried potatoes and cauliflower to the pan and mix gently to coat with the spices.
Add salt, cover the pan, and cook on low heat for 10-15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until vegetables are fully cooked.
Sprinkle amchur powder and garam masala over the vegetables and mix well.
Garnish with chopped coriander leaves and serve hot with phulka or paratha.

name: Aloo Paratha
instructions: In a large bowl, mix whole wheat flour with half a teaspoon of salt. Gradually add water to knead a soft, smooth dough. Cover and let it rest for 15 minutes.
Mash the boiled potatoes thoroughly so there are no lumps.
Mix the mashed potatoes with chopped onions, green chilli, ginger, coriander leaves, red chilli powder, garam masala, amchur powder, and the remaining salt.
Divide the rested dough into 4-6 equal balls.
Take a dough ball, dust with dry flour, and roll it out into a 4-inch circle.
Place a generous portion of the potato filling in the center.
Bring the edges of the dough together over the filling and pinch to seal completely.
Flatten slightly, dust with dry flour, and gently roll out into an 8-inch paratha, being careful not to let the filling spill out.
Heat a tawa (griddle) on medium heat. Place the rolled paratha on it.
Cook until slight brown spots appear on the bottom, then flip. Apply half a teaspoon of ghee over the surface.
Flip again, apply ghee to the other side, and press gently with a spatula until both sides are golden and crispy.
Serve hot with a dollop of white butter, pickle, and thick curd.

name: Aloo Posto

ingredients.notes: peeled and cut into small cubes
posto, soaked in warm water for 30 minutes

instructions: Drain the soaked poppy seeds (posto) and grind them into a smooth, thick paste along with two green chillies and a tiny splash of water.
Heat mustard oil in a heavy-bottomed pan until it reaches smoking point, then lower the heat.
Add one slit green chilli to the oil and sauté for a few seconds.
Add the potato cubes and fry on medium heat for 5-6 minutes until they get a light golden crust.
Add salt, sugar, and half a cup of water. Cover the pan and cook until the potatoes are 80% tender.
Remove the lid, pour the prepared poppy seed paste into the pan, and mix gently to coat the potatoes.
Cook uncovered on low heat for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the raw smell of the poppy seeds disappears and the dish looks relatively dry.
Drizzle a few drops of raw mustard oil on top for an authentic pungent kick (optional) and turn off the heat.
Serve warm with steamed rice and musur dal.

name: Aloo Pyaz Ki Sabzi

ingredients.notes: small baby onions left whole, or medium onions quartered

instructions: Heat the mustard oil in a heavy kadai until it reaches smoking point. Turn down the heat slightly.
Carefully shallow fry the potato cubes in the oil until golden and half cooked. Remove and set aside.
In the same oil, shallow fry the whole baby onions (or quartered onions) for 2-3 minutes until they gain a light color. Remove and set aside.
In the remaining oil, add cumin seeds. When they splutter, add the ginger and garlic paste and saute for a minute.
Pour in the tomato puree along with turmeric, red chilli powder, coriander powder, and salt. Cook until oil separates from the masala.
Return the fried potatoes and onions to the pan. Mix well so the masala coats the vegetables.
Add 1 cup of warm water, cover the pan, and let it simmer for 10-12 minutes until the potatoes are completely tender.
Sprinkle amchur powder and garam masala. Mix gently to keep the onions intact.
Garnish with fresh coriander leaves and serve hot with phulkas.

name: Amritsari Chole

ingredients.notes: tied in a muslin cloth pouch

instructions: In a pressure cooker, add soaked kabuli chana, salt, the tied tea leaves pouch, and 3 cups of water.
Pressure cook for 5-6 whistles until the chickpeas are very tender. Discard the tea pouch and reserve the dark water.
Heat oil in a heavy kadai. Add cumin seeds and let them crackle.
Add the onion paste and fry until it turns dark brown and oil separates.
Add ginger-garlic paste and sauté for another 2 minutes until the raw smell goes away.
Stir in the tomato puree and cook until the masala thickens and leaves oil on the sides.
Add coriander powder, red chilli powder, amchur powder, and garam masala. Mix well and roast the spices for a minute.
Add the boiled chickpeas along with the dark reserved water.
Simmer on medium-low heat for 15-20 minutes, lightly mashing some chickpeas against the pan to thicken the gravy.
Serve hot with bhatura, kulcha, or jeera rice.

name: Andhra Style Spinach Dal

ingredients.notes: small lump soaked, mapped from raw tamarind to pulp

instructions: In a pressure cooker, add the soaked toor dal, chopped spinach, tomato, onion, green chillies, turmeric powder, and 2 cups of water.
Close the lid and pressure cook for 4 whistles on medium heat until the dal and greens are completely soft.
Let the pressure release naturally. Open the cooker and lightly mash the dal and spinach mixture.
Mix the tamarind pulp with a little warm water to dissolve, then add to the mashed dal along with salt.
Simmer the dal mixture on low heat for 5 minutes so the raw tamarind flavor cooks out.
For the tempering, heat sunflower oil in a small pan. Add mustard seeds and cumin. Let them splutter.
Add the crushed garlic and dried red chillies, frying for a few seconds until the garlic is fragrant and lightly browned.
Pour the hot tempering over the simmering dal, mix well, and serve hot with steamed rice.

name: Andhra Tomato Stew

ingredients.notes: gooseberry-size raw tamarind mapped to pulp, soaked

instructions: Mix the tamarind pulp with 1 cup of water and stir well to make tamarind extract.
Heat the sunflower oil in a deep pot or kadai over medium heat.
Add mustard seeds, cumin, fenugreek seeds, and dried red chilli. Let them splutter.
Add the curry leaves, slit green chillies, and thick onion slices. Sauté for 2-3 minutes until the onions turn slightly pink but retain their crunch.
Add the chopped tomatoes, turmeric powder, red chilli powder, and salt. Cook until the tomatoes are fully soft and mushy.
Pour the tamarind extract along with an additional 1 cup of water into the pot.
Add the crushed jaggery and stir well to balance the tanginess.
Bring the pulusu to a rolling boil, then lower the heat and simmer for 10 minutes until it slightly thickens. Garnish with coriander leaves and serve with hot rice.

name: Baked Baati

ingredients.notes: 3 tbsp for dough, 1 tbsp for coating/serving

instructions: In a large mixing bowl, combine whole wheat flour, semolina, besan, crushed ajwain, and salt.
Add 3 tablespoons of melted ghee to the flour mixture. Rub the ghee into the flour using your fingertips until it resembles coarse breadcrumbs.
Gradually add warm water and knead into a stiff, tight dough (stiffer than roti dough). Let it rest for 15 minutes.
Preheat your oven to 180C (350F) or prepare a gas tandoor.
Divide the rested dough into equal lemon-sized balls. Roll them between your palms and flatten slightly, making a small indentation in the center with your thumb.
Place the baatis on a baking tray. Bake for 30-40 minutes, flipping them halfway, until they are golden brown and cooked from the inside with visible cracks.
Once baked, lightly crush each hot baati to open it up slightly.
Drizzle with the remaining ghee. Serve immediately with Panchmel Dal.

name: Bandhakopir Ghonto
instructions: Heat mustard oil in a large pan until it smokes, then reduce the heat.
Add the potato cubes, fry until golden brown, and set them aside.
In the remaining oil, add bay leaf and cumin seeds. Allow them to splutter.
Add grated ginger and slit green chillies, sautéing until aromatic.
Add the shredded cabbage along with turmeric, red chilli powder, coriander powder, and salt. Mix well.
Cover the pan and cook on medium-low heat for about 10 minutes until the cabbage releases its water and shrinks.
Add the fried potatoes and green peas, mixing everything thoroughly.
Cover again and cook for another 10-15 minutes until the vegetables are completely tender and the moisture evaporates.
Add sugar and ghee, stir-frying on medium heat for 2-3 minutes.
Sprinkle garam masala, mix well, and turn off the heat.
Serve hot with luchi, paratha, or rice.

name: Batata poha
instructions: Rinse the flattened rice in a sieve under running water, drain out all excess water, and set aside to puff up.
Peel the potato and cut it into very small uniform cubes.
Heat the oil in a pan and fry the peanuts until lightly browned and crisp, then push to one side.
Add mustard seeds and let them crackle; add curry leaves and chopped green chilli.
Add the diced potato cubes, cover and cook on low heat until fork-tender.
Add the chopped onion and saute until translucent.
Stir in turmeric powder, salt, and sugar; cook for thirty seconds.
Fluff the softened flattened rice and add to the pan; toss gently to combine, cover and steam on low for three minutes, then finish with lemon juice and serve.

name: Bengali aloo chachchari
instructions: Peel the potatoes and cut into uniform small cubes; rinse and drain.
Heat mustard oil in a kadhai until it smokes lightly, then lower the flame.
Add cumin, fennel and fenugreek seeds; let them crackle for ten seconds.
Add the slit green chillies and the potato cubes; toss to coat in the tempered oil.
Sprinkle turmeric powder and salt, stirring to coat the potatoes evenly.
Add half a cup of water, cover the pan, and simmer on low heat for ten minutes.
Uncover and mash a few cubes against the side of the pan to thicken the gravy.
Cook uncovered for two more minutes until the moisture clings to the potatoes and serve hot with luchi or rice.

name: Bengali Niramish aloor dum
instructions: Boil the potatoes until firm-cooked, peel, and halve into large pieces.
Heat mustard oil in a kadhai until it smokes, then reduce the flame.
Add asafoetida, cumin seeds and bay leaf; let them sizzle for fifteen seconds.
Add grated ginger and chopped green chilli; sauté for thirty seconds until aromatic.
Add the chopped tomato along with turmeric, red chilli powder and salt; cook until the tomato breaks down into a thick mash.
Add the boiled potato halves and toss gently to coat them in the masala.
Pour half a cup of water, cover, and simmer on low flame for five to seven minutes.
Uncover, reduce until the masala clings thickly to the potatoes, sprinkle garam masala and chopped coriander, and serve with luchi or paratha.

name: Bharela Ringan Batata
instructions: Wash the small brinjals and peeled potatoes. Make a deep cross-slit in each, keeping the base intact so they hold the stuffing.
In a mixing bowl, combine besan, crushed peanuts, sesame seeds, coriander powder, turmeric powder, red chilli powder, sugar, and salt.
Add minced ginger, garlic, green chillies, chopped coriander leaves, and 1 tablespoon of groundnut oil to the dry spice mix. Rub well to form a slightly moist stuffing.
Carefully open the slits and stuff this masala mixture into the brinjals and potatoes. Reserve any leftover masala.
Heat the remaining groundnut oil in a heavy-bottomed wide pan or pressure cooker over medium heat.
Gently place the stuffed vegetables into the hot oil and shallow fry them for 2-3 minutes.
Sprinkle the reserved stuffing masala evenly over the top and carefully pour in half a cup of water around the edges (not directly over the veggies).
Cover with a lid and cook on low heat for 20-25 minutes (or 2 whistles if using a pressure cooker) until the vegetables are completely tender.
Garnish with a little more fresh coriander leaves and serve hot with phulka or bhakri.

name: Bharli Vangi

ingredients.notes: used as substitute for goda masala

instructions: Wash the baby eggplants, keep the stems, and make two cross slits from the base up to the stem (do not cut entirely). Soak them in salted water for 10 minutes.

In a bowl, prepare the stuffing by mixing crushed peanuts, roasted sesame seeds, minced garlic, grated ginger, garam masala, coriander powder, red chilli powder, turmeric, salt, half of the jaggery, and chopped coriander leaves.
Remove the eggplants from water, pat them dry, and gently stuff the prepared dry masala mixture into the slits of each eggplant. Reserve the leftover masala.
Heat groundnut oil in a heavy-bottomed pan. Add the chopped onions and sauté until golden brown.
Add the chopped tomatoes and cook until they are soft and mushy.
Place the stuffed eggplants gently into the pan. Sauté carefully for 2-3 minutes so the outer skin blisters slightly.
Add the reserved leftover stuffing masala, tamarind pulp, the remaining jaggery, and 1.5 cups of warm water. Mix gently around the eggplants.
Cover the pan with a lid and cook on medium-low heat for 15-20 minutes until the eggplants are completely tender and oil floats on top.
Garnish with more coriander leaves and serve hot with chapati or bhakri.

name: Bhindi Masala

ingredients.notes: washed, completely dried, and cut into 1-inch pieces

instructions: Rinse the okra and pat them completely dry with a kitchen towel before chopping to prevent sliminess.
Heat the mustard oil in a pan until it smokes, then lower the heat.
Add cumin seeds and let them splutter.
Add the sliced onions and sauté until they start to turn golden brown.
Add the chopped okra pieces to the pan. Cook on medium heat for 7-8 minutes, stirring occasionally without covering the pan.
Once the okra loses its stickiness and is almost cooked, add the turmeric and red chilli powder.
Stir in the chopped tomatoes and cook for another 3-4 minutes until they soften slightly.
Finally, add the salt, garam masala, and amchur powder. Mix gently.
Cook for 2 more minutes to let the flavors blend. Remove from heat and serve hot with phulkas.

name: Bisi Bele Bath

ingredients.notes: small stick, dry roasted and powdered

instructions: In a pressure cooker, add washed rice, toor dal, carrots, french beans, green peas, and 4 cups of water.
Cook for 4-5 whistles until everything is soft and mushy. Mash lightly and set aside.
In a small pan, dry roast coriander seeds, chana dal, cinnamon, cloves, and dried red chillies until fragrant. Grind them into a fine powder (bisi bele bath masala).
In a large heavy-bottomed pot, bring the tamarind extract to a boil and let it cook for 5 minutes.
Add the ground spice powder and salt to the tamarind extract, mixing well.
Pour the cooked rice-dal-vegetable mixture into the pot. Add water if it is too thick.
Simmer the entire mixture on low heat for 5-7 minutes so the flavors merge.
In a separate small pan, heat ghee. Fry peanuts until golden, then add mustard seeds and curry leaves.
Pour this hot tempering over the Bisi Bele Bath and mix well.
Serve steaming hot with potato chips or boondi.

name: Cabbage Poriyal
instructions: Heat sunflower oil in a wide pan or wok over medium heat.
Add mustard seeds. Once they splutter, add the raw urad dal and chana dal. Roast until the dals turn a light golden color.
Add the slit green chilli and curry leaves, letting them sizzle for a few seconds.
Add the finely chopped onion and sauté until it becomes translucent.
Stir in the shredded cabbage, turmeric powder, and salt. Mix well so the tempering coats the cabbage.
Cover the pan and cook on low heat for 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the cabbage is tender but retains a slight crunch. Serve hot.

name: Cabbage Watana Shaak
instructions: Heat sunflower oil in a kadai or wide pan over medium heat.
Add mustard seeds and wait for them to crackle, then add cumin seeds and asafoetida.
Add the finely chopped green chillies and sauté for a few seconds.
Add the shredded cabbage and green peas to the pan. Toss well.
Sprinkle turmeric powder, red chilli powder, coriander powder, salt, and sugar over the vegetables.
Toss everything together to coat the cabbage and peas evenly with the spices.
Cover the pan with a lid that has a little water poured on top (this creates steam to cook the sabzi without adding water directly into the pan).
Cook on low heat for 10-12 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the cabbage is tender but retains a slight crunch.
Garnish with freshly chopped coriander leaves and serve hot with roti, dal, and rice.

name: Chettinad Egg Curry
instructions: Make shallow vertical slits on the hard-boiled eggs so they can absorb the curry flavors. Set aside.
Heat the sunflower oil in a pan over medium heat. Add the mustard seeds, fennel seeds, and cumin. Let them splutter.
Add the curry leaves and finely chopped onions. Sauté until the onions turn golden brown.
Add the ginger and garlic paste, cooking for 2 minutes until the raw aroma completely disappears.
Stir in the finely chopped tomatoes and cook until they break down into a mushy paste.
Lower the heat and add the turmeric powder, red chilli powder, coriander powder, freshly crushed black pepper, and salt. Sauté for 2 minutes until oil separates.
Pour in 1.5 cups of water to adjust the consistency of the gravy, bringing it to a simmer.
Gently drop the boiled eggs into the simmering gravy. Cover and cook on low heat for 8-10 minutes so the spices infuse into the eggs.
Turn off the heat and serve the flavorful Chettinad egg curry with chapati or rice.

name: Cholar Dal
instructions: Pressure cook the soaked chana dal with 2.5 cups of water, turmeric powder, and a pinch of salt for 4-5 whistles until cooked soft but holding its shape.
In a kadai or deep pan, heat the ghee over medium heat.
Add the bay leaf, dried red chillies, and cumin seeds. Let the cumin seeds splutter.
Add the grated ginger and slit green chillies, sautéing for about a minute until fragrant.
Pour the cooked dal into the pan. If the dal is too thick, add half a cup of warm water.
Add sugar and the remaining salt. Mix well (Bengali cholar dal is traditionally a little sweet).
Bring the dal to a gentle simmer and let it cook for 5-6 minutes to blend the flavors.
Sprinkle the garam masala powder over the dal and stir well.
Turn off the heat and serve hot with luchi, puri, or steamed rice.

name: Chole Masala

ingredients.notes: tied in muslin, boiled with chickpeas for colour

instructions: Pressure cook the soaked kabuli chana with enough water, the bay leaf, the muslin pouch of tea leaves and a pinch of salt until soft; discard the tea pouch.
Heat oil in a heavy pan. Add cumin seeds and let them splutter.
Add chopped onions and sauté until golden brown.
Add ginger and garlic, sautéing until the raw smell disappears.
Pour in the tomato puree and cook until the oil starts leaving the sides of the masala.
Lower the heat and add coriander powder, red chilli powder, and salt. Sauté for 1-2 minutes.
Add the boiled chickpeas along with some of the cooking liquid.
Simmer for 15 minutes, lightly mashing some chickpeas with the back of a spoon to thicken the gravy.
Stir in the garam masala and amchur powder.
Cook for another 2 minutes, remove from heat, and serve with rice, bhature, or roti.

name: Curd Rice

ingredients.notes: raw rice, to be cooked mushy

instructions: Pressure cook the sona masoori rice with 2 cups of water for 4-5 whistles so it becomes very soft and mushy.
While the rice is still hot, mash it well with a spoon. Let it cool down to room temperature.
Once cooled, add the curd, milk, and salt to the mashed rice. Mix thoroughly until creamy.
In a small pan, heat sunflower oil for the tempering.
Add mustard seeds and let them splutter. Add urad dal and fry until golden brown.
Add the finely minced ginger, chopped green chilli, and curry leaves. Sauté for a few seconds.
Pour this tempering over the prepared curd rice and mix well.
Serve chilled or at room temperature, ideally with a side of pickle or pappadam.

name: Dal Makhani
instructions: Drain the soaked whole urad and rajma. Pressure cook with 4 cups of water and half a teaspoon of salt for 6-8 whistles until very soft and mushy.
Lightly mash the cooked lentils against the side of the cooker with a spoon.
Heat butter in a heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat.
Add cumin seeds and let them splutter. Add minced ginger and garlic, sautéing until aromatic.
Add finely chopped onions and cook until they turn golden brown.
Pour in the tomato puree along with red chilli powder. Cook until the butter separates from the masala.
Transfer the mashed dal along with its cooking liquid into the pot.
Mix well and let it simmer on low heat for at least 30 to 45 minutes. The longer it simmers, the creamier it gets. Add warm water if it thickens too much.
Stir in garam masala, crushed dried fenugreek leaves (kasuri methi), and fresh cream.
Simmer for another 5 minutes. Serve hot with naan or jeera rice.

name: Dal Tadka
instructions: In a pressure cooker, add the washed toor dal, moong dal, turmeric powder, and 3 cups of water. Cook for 3-4 whistles until completely mushy.
Whisk the cooked dal until smooth. Adjust consistency with warm water if it's too thick, and add salt.
In a small pan, heat ghee for the tempering (tadka).
Add mustard seeds and let them pop, then add cumin seeds, dried red chillies, and minced garlic.
Sauté until the garlic turns lightly golden.
Add the chopped onions and green chilli, sautéing until the onions soften.
Add the tomatoes and cook until they break down and become mushy.
Pour this hot tempering over the cooked dal and mix well.
Simmer the dal for 2-3 minutes to allow flavors to blend.
Garnish with fresh coriander leaves and serve hot with rice or roti.

name: Dalia upma
instructions: Dry-roast the broken wheat in a pan over medium flame for four to five minutes until it turns aromatic, then set aside.
Heat groundnut oil in a pressure cooker, add mustard seeds and cumin, and let them splutter.
Add curry leaves, grated ginger, and chopped green chilli; saute briefly.
Add chopped onion and saute until translucent, then add chopped carrot and french beans and cook for two minutes.
Add turmeric powder, salt, and the roasted broken wheat; stir to combine.
Pour in two and a half cups of water and stir well.
Close the pressure cooker and cook for two whistles on medium heat, then turn off and let pressure release naturally.
Open, fluff the dalia upma gently with a fork, and serve hot.

name: Dhaba Style Aloo Gobi
instructions: Heat the mustard oil in a heavy bottomed pan until it reaches smoking point, then lower the heat slightly.
Add the cubed potatoes and cauliflower florets to the pan. Fry them for 5-7 minutes until lightly golden. Remove and set aside.
In the same remaining oil, add cumin seeds and let them splutter.
Add finely chopped onion and sauté until golden brown.
Stir in the julienned ginger and slit green chilli, cooking for another minute.
Add the chopped tomatoes, turmeric, and red chilli powder. Cook until the tomatoes are mushy and oil starts separating from the masala.
Return the fried potatoes and cauliflower to the pan. Add salt and mix well so the vegetables are coated in the masala.
Cover the pan with a lid and cook on low heat for 10-12 minutes, stirring occasionally, until vegetables are fully tender.
Sprinkle garam masala and chopped coriander leaves over the top. Mix gently to avoid mashing the vegetables.
Serve hot with rotis or parathas.

name: Drumstick and Bottle Gourd Sambar

ingredients.notes: to be dry roasted and ground for fresh sambar masala
to be dry roasted and ground
to be dry roasted and ground
to be dry roasted and ground

instructions: Pressure cook the toor dal with turmeric powder and 2 cups of water for 4 whistles until fully soft. Mash well and set aside.
In a small pan, dry roast the coriander seeds, cumin, fenugreek seeds, and dried red chilli on low heat until fragrant. Cool and grind into a fine fresh sambar powder.
In a large heavy-bottomed pot, boil the drumstick pieces, bottle gourd cubes, chopped onions, and tomatoes with 2 cups of water and salt.
Once the vegetables are half cooked (about 10 minutes), pour in the extracted tamarind juice.
Add the freshly ground sambar powder to the boiling vegetables. Stir well to ensure no lumps form.
Continue to boil for another 5-7 minutes until the raw smell of tamarind goes away and the vegetables are completely tender.
Pour the mashed toor dal into the pot. Mix well and let the sambar simmer on low heat for 5 minutes.
In a separate small pan, heat the sunflower oil for tempering. Add mustard seeds and let them splutter.
Add the curry leaves and asafoetida to the hot oil, let it sizzle for 5 seconds, then immediately pour this over the simmering sambar.
Mix well, turn off the heat, cover, and let the flavors meld for a few minutes before serving with rice or dosa.

name: Ennai Kathirikai Kuzhambu

ingredients.notes: small brinjals, slit into 4 leaving the stalk intact
soaked and extracted into 1.5 cups water

instructions: Heat 1 tablespoon of sesame oil in a pan. Add the slit brinjals and sauté for 5-6 minutes until they blister and turn slightly tender. Remove and set aside.
In the same pan, heat the remaining sesame oil. Add mustard seeds and let them splutter.
Add fenugreek seeds, curry leaves, and garlic cloves. Sauté until garlic is light brown.
Add the finely chopped onions and sauté until translucent.
Add the chopped tomatoes and cook until they break down completely and oil separates.
Lower the heat and add turmeric powder, red chilli powder, and coriander powder. Mix quickly.
Pour in the tamarind extract and add salt. Bring the mixture to a rolling boil.
Gently slide in the sautéed brinjals into the boiling curry.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 10-12 minutes until the oil floats on top and the curry has thickened.
Serve hot with steamed rice and a side of appalam (papad).

name: Gatte Ki Sabzi
instructions: In a bowl, mix besan with ajwain, half the turmeric, half the red chilli powder, a pinch of salt, and 1 tablespoon of ghee. Add a little water to knead into a stiff dough.
Divide the dough into equal parts and roll them into long cylindrical logs (about half an inch thick).
Boil 3 cups of water in a wide pan. Drop the logs into the boiling water and cook for 10-12 minutes until they float and have small blisters on the surface.
Remove the logs from the water, let them cool, and cut them into 1-inch discs (gatte). Reserve the boiling water for the gravy.
In a separate pan, heat the remaining 1 tablespoon of ghee. Add cumin seeds and let them splutter.
Add finely chopped onions and saute until golden brown. Stir in ginger and garlic paste, cooking until the raw smell goes away.
Add the chopped tomatoes, remaining turmeric, red chilli powder, coriander powder, and salt. Cook until tomatoes are mushy and oil separates.
Lower the heat completely and whisk the curd into the masala continuously to prevent it from curdling. Cook for 3-4 minutes.
Pour the reserved boiling water into the gravy and bring to a simmer. Drop the gatte pieces in.
Simmer the curry for 8-10 minutes until the gravy thickens slightly. Garnish with garam masala and coriander leaves. Serve hot with roti.

name: Gobi paratha
instructions: Grate the cauliflower florets finely; squeeze in a clean cloth to remove excess moisture.
Combine the grated cauliflower, onion, green chilli, coriander leaves, cumin, and salt in a mixing bowl for the stuffing.
Knead whole wheat flour with water into a soft dough, then rest it for five minutes.
Divide the dough into two equal balls and flatten each into a small thick disc.
Place half of the cauliflower mixture in the center of a disc, bring the edges together, and pinch to seal.
Gently roll the stuffed ball into a flat circular paratha using dry flour for dusting.
Place the paratha on a preheated tawa and cook on medium flame until bubbles appear.
Flip, drizzle oil around the edges, and cook the other side until golden spots form and the paratha is thoroughly cooked.

name: Gujarati Dal
instructions: Wash and pressure cook the toor dal along with the raw peanuts and 2 cups of water for 4-5 whistles until very soft.
Mash the cooked dal smoothly. Add chopped tomatoes, grated ginger, and slit green chillies to the pot.
Add turmeric powder, red chilli powder, coriander powder, salt, and jaggery.
Pour in 1.5 cups of water to adjust the consistency to medium-thin, and boil the dal for 10-12 minutes on medium heat.
In a small tempering pan, heat ghee. Add mustard seeds, cumin seeds, and fenugreek seeds. Let them crackle.
Add cloves, cinnamon, dried red chillies, and curry leaves. Sauté for a few seconds until fragrant.
Carefully pour the hot tempering into the boiling dal and mix well.
Simmer for another 5 minutes to let the sweet, sour, and spicy flavors blend.
Turn off the heat, stir in the freshly squeezed lemon juice, and garnish with coriander leaves. Serve hot with rice or roti.

name: Gujarati Kadhi
instructions: In a large bowl, whisk the curd and besan together until completely smooth and lump-free.
Add 2.5 cups of water, salt, and sugar to the curd mixture and whisk well.
Transfer the mixture to a heavy-bottomed pot and bring it to a gentle boil on medium heat, stirring continuously to prevent curdling.
Once it boils, add the grated ginger and chopped green chilli. Lower the heat and let it simmer for 10 minutes.
In a small pan, heat ghee for the tempering. Add mustard seeds and let them pop.
Add cumin seeds, fenugreek seeds, cloves, and cinnamon stick. Sauté for a few seconds until fragrant.
Add curry leaves and immediately pour this hot tempering into the simmering kadhi.
Mix well, simmer for 2 more minutes, and turn off the heat.
Garnish with chopped coriander leaves and serve hot with khichdi.

name: Homestyle Chicken Curry
instructions: Heat mustard oil in a heavy-bottomed pot until it smokes, then turn down the heat.
Add bay leaf, cinnamon stick, and cumin seeds. Let them crackle for a few seconds.
Add the finely chopped onions and sauté patiently until they turn dark golden brown.
Stir in the ginger and garlic paste and cook for 2 minutes until the raw smell is gone.
Add the tomato puree along with turmeric, red chilli powder, ground coriander seeds, and salt.
Cook this masala on medium heat until the oil separates from the edges.
Add the chicken pieces and fry them in the masala on high heat for 5-7 minutes to seal the juices.
Add 1.5 cups of warm water, mix well, and bring to a boil.
Cover the pot, lower the heat, and simmer for 20-25 minutes until the chicken is tender and cooked through.
Sprinkle garam masala and garnish with fresh coriander leaves. Serve hot with roti or rice.

name: Jeera Rice
instructions: Wash the basmati rice gently under running water and soak it for 20 minutes, then drain completely.
Heat ghee in a deep pan or pot over medium heat.
Add cumin seeds to the hot ghee. Wait until they splutter and turn a slightly dark brown color to release maximum flavor.
Add the drained basmati rice to the pan and gently sauté for 1-2 minutes until the grains are coated with ghee.
Pour in 2 cups of water and add the salt. Stir gently.
Bring the water to a rolling boil, then lower the heat to a gentle simmer.
Cover the pan with a tight-fitting lid and cook undisturbed for 10-12 minutes.
Turn off the heat and let the rice rest covered for another 5 minutes.
Fluff the rice gently with a fork.
Garnish with chopped coriander leaves and serve hot.

name: Jowar Bhakri
instructions: Boil 1 cup of water in a pot. Once it comes to a rolling boil, turn off the heat.
In a wide mixing bowl, combine the sorghum (jowar) flour and salt.
Gradually pour the hot water into the flour, mixing it initially with a spoon as it will be very hot.
Once cool enough to handle, knead the mixture vigorously with the heel of your palm for 5-7 minutes to form a smooth, crack-free dough. This is crucial for gluten-free flours.
Divide the dough into 4 equal portions and shape them into smooth balls.
Heat a cast-iron tawa (griddle) over medium-high heat.
Dust your rolling surface with a little dry jowar flour. Place a dough ball and flatten it gently using the palm and fingers of your hand into a round, even flatbread (about 6-7 inches wide).
Carefully lift the bhakri and place it on the hot tawa, with the flour-dusted side facing upwards.
Immediately apply a thin layer of water over the top surface using a clean damp cloth or your fingers.
Wait 10-15 seconds for the water to evaporate slightly, then flip the bhakri. Roast the other side until brown spots appear, then flip again and press gently with a cloth so it puffs up. Serve hot.

name: Kadai Paneer
instructions: In a dry pan, roast coriander seeds, dried red chillies, and cumin until fragrant. Let them cool, then grind into a coarse powder (Kadai Masala).
Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a pan or kadai. Add the diced onion and capsicum squares. Sauté on high heat for 3-4 minutes until they have slight blister marks but remain crunchy. Remove and set aside.
In the same pan, heat the remaining oil. Add minced garlic and ginger, sautéing for a minute.
Add the tomato puree and cook until the oil starts separating from the edges.
Mix in turmeric powder, salt, and 2 tablespoons of the freshly ground Kadai Masala. Cook for another 2 minutes.
Add half a cup of water to create a thick gravy base.
Gently slide in the paneer cubes, sautéed onions, and capsicum.
Toss well so the masala coats everything. Simmer for 3-4 minutes on low heat.
Sprinkle garam masala and crushed dried fenugreek leaves on top. Serve immediately with hot roti or paratha.

name: Kanda poha maharashtrian
instructions: Place the flattened rice into a colander, wash it gently under running water, drain completely, and leave to soften.
Heat groundnut oil in a pan and fry the peanuts until lightly browned and crisp, then push them to one side.
Add mustard seeds and let them crackle, then add curry leaves and chopped green chilli.
Add the chopped onion and saute on medium heat until translucent and soft.
Stir in the turmeric powder, salt, and sugar; cook for thirty seconds.
Gently fluff the softened flattened rice with your fingers and add it to the pan, tossing carefully from the bottom to coat without breaking the flakes.
Cover the pan with a tight lid and steam on low heat for three minutes.
Turn off the heat, finish with lemon juice and chopped coriander leaves, mix gently, and serve.

name: Kerala Pepper Chicken Roast
instructions: Marinate the chicken pieces with turmeric powder, half of the salt, and half of the freshly ground black pepper for 15 minutes.
Heat the coconut oil in a heavy-bottomed pan or kadai over medium-high heat.
Add one sprig of curry leaves, followed immediately by the thinly sliced onions. Sauté patiently until the onions turn deep golden brown.
Add the crushed ginger and garlic, cooking for 2 minutes until the raw smell vanishes.
Stir in the chopped tomatoes and cook until they break down entirely and oil begins to separate.
Add the marinated chicken pieces to the pan. Sear them on high heat for 5 minutes, turning frequently to brown all sides.
Lower the heat, cover the pan, and let the chicken cook in its own juices for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally. Add a splash of water only if it sticks.
Once the chicken is fully cooked, add the remaining black pepper, fennel powder, remaining salt, and the second sprig of curry leaves.
Increase the heat and roast (fry) the chicken for another 5 minutes until the masala is dark, thick, and coats the chicken completely.

name: Lemon Rice

ingredients.notes: raw rice, cooked with separate grains

instructions: Cook the sona masoori rice so the grains remain separate. Spread it on a wide plate and let it cool completely.
Heat sesame oil in a wide pan over medium heat. Add peanuts and fry until they are crisp and golden. Remove and set aside.
In the same oil, add mustard seeds. Once they splutter, add chana dal and urad dal.
Fry until the dals turn a light golden color.
Add slit green chillies, curry leaves, and asafoetida. Sauté for a few seconds.
Turn the heat to the lowest setting. Add turmeric powder and mix quickly.
Turn off the heat and stir in the freshly squeezed lemon juice and salt.
Add the cooled rice and fried peanuts to the pan.
Gently toss and mix everything until the rice is evenly coated with the yellow color and spices.
Let the rice rest for 10-15 minutes before serving so the flavors are absorbed.

name: Maharashtrian Pithla

ingredients.notes: crushed cloves in a mortar and pestle

instructions: In a mixing bowl, combine the besan with 2.5 cups of water. Whisk vigorously to ensure there are no lumps to form a smooth slurry.
Heat the groundnut oil in a heavy-bottomed pan over medium heat.
Add mustard seeds and let them pop. Then add cumin seeds, asafoetida, and the crushed garlic.
Sauté for a few seconds until the garlic turns lightly golden and aromatic.
Add the chopped green chillies and finely chopped onions. Sauté until the onions turn soft and translucent.
Stir in the turmeric powder and salt, mixing well.
Reduce the heat to low. Slowly pour the besan slurry into the pan while stirring continuously with your other hand to prevent lumps from forming.
Cook the mixture on low heat for 5-7 minutes, stirring often. It will begin to thicken quickly and turn slightly glossy.
Once the pithla leaves the sides of the pan slightly and tastes completely cooked (no raw besan flavor), turn off the heat.
Garnish generously with freshly chopped coriander leaves. Serve piping hot with Jowar Bhakri and raw onion on the side.

name: Maharashtrian Sadha Varan

ingredients.notes: crushed, optional for slight sweetness (Goda Varan)

instructions: In a pressure cooker, add the washed toor dal, turmeric powder, a few drops of ghee, and 2 cups of water.
Pressure cook for 4-5 whistles on medium heat until the dal is completely soft and mushy.
Let the pressure release naturally. Open the cooker and whisk the dal well until perfectly smooth.
Add the salt, crushed jaggery, and an extra half cup of water to adjust the consistency. Bring to a gentle simmer for 3 minutes.
In a small tempering pan, heat the remaining ghee. Add cumin seeds and let them splutter.
Add asafoetida and curry leaves to the hot ghee, letting them sizzle for 5 seconds.
Pour this hot tempering over the simmering dal. Turn off the heat.
Garnish with freshly chopped coriander leaves and serve hot with steamed rice (Varan-Bhat).

name: Matar Paneer
instructions: In a pan, heat a little oil and sauté onions, tomatoes, ginger, garlic, and cashews until tomatoes are soft.
Allow the mixture to cool, then blend it into a smooth paste using a little water.
In the same pan, heat the remaining oil. Add the blended paste and cook for 5-7 minutes on medium heat.
Add turmeric, red chilli powder, and coriander powder. Sauté until the oil separates from the masala.
Add the green peas, salt, and about 1 cup of water. Stir well.
Cover and simmer for 8-10 minutes until the peas are cooked and tender.
Add the paneer cubes, garam masala, and kasuri methi.
Simmer for an additional 3-4 minutes to let the paneer absorb the flavors.
Serve hot with paratha, roti, or pulao.

name: Matar poha
instructions: Rinse the flattened rice thoroughly in a sieve, drain all water, and let it rest to become soft.
Heat groundnut oil in a pan, add mustard seeds and let them crackle.
Add curry leaves, chopped onion, and green chilli; saute until onion softens.
Add green peas and a splash of water, cover and cook for three to four minutes until peas are tender.
Stir in turmeric powder and salt.
Gently add the softened flattened rice and toss to combine evenly with the vegetables.
Cover and steam on low heat for three minutes.
Finish with lemon juice and chopped coriander leaves, and serve warm.

name: Matki Usal

ingredients.notes: soaked for 6 hours, ideally sprouted overnight

instructions: Rinse the sprouted/soaked matki beans under running water. Drain completely.
Heat groundnut oil in a pan over medium heat. Add mustard seeds and cumin seeds. Allow them to splutter.
Add asafoetida and curry leaves, followed by the minced garlic and grated ginger. Sauté for a few seconds until fragrant.
Add the finely chopped onion and sauté until it turns translucent and soft.
Stir in the chopped tomatoes, turmeric powder, and red chilli powder. Cook until the tomatoes are completely soft and oil starts releasing from the sides.
Add the sprouted matki beans and mix them well into the onion-tomato masala.
Pour in 1.5 to 2 cups of water, add salt, and bring the curry to a boil.
Cover and simmer on medium-low heat for 12-15 minutes until the matki is tender but not mushy.
Stir in the garam masala and crushed jaggery. Simmer for another 2 minutes to balance the flavors.
Garnish with chopped coriander leaves and serve hot with pav, bhakri, or chapati.

name: Methi paratha
instructions: Wash the fenugreek leaves thoroughly, drain completely, and chop them very finely.
Finely chop the onion and green chilli.
In a large bowl, combine whole wheat flour, chopped fenugreek leaves, chopped onion, green chilli, ajwain, turmeric, and salt.
Mix well and gradually add water to knead into a firm yet soft dough.
Divide the kneaded dough into two equal portions and shape into round balls.
Roll out each ball into a round paratha on a lightly floured surface.
Place the paratha on a preheated griddle on medium heat.
Flip, drizzle oil around the edges, and cook the other side, pressing gently until both sides are well cooked.

name: Methi paratha west style
instructions: Clean the fenugreek leaves carefully, wash thoroughly to remove grit, drain, and chop fine.
Finely chop the green chilli and grate the ginger.
In a large bowl, combine whole wheat flour, besan, chopped fenugreek leaves, green chilli, grated ginger, ajwain, turmeric, and salt.
Rub the greens and spices into the flour, then add curd and 6g of oil and mix well.
Gradually add water and knead into a firm, smooth, slightly tacky dough; rest for ten minutes.
Divide the dough into two equal balls and roll each out into an even round flatbread using dry flour for dusting.
Heat a tawa over medium-high heat and place the rolled paratha on it.
Cook until small bubbles appear, flip and drizzle a little oil around the edges; cook both sides until well browned with golden spots.

name: Methi thepla
instructions: Pick and wash the fresh fenugreek leaves thoroughly, then chop them very finely.
Pound the green chilli and ginger into a smooth paste using a mortar and pestle.
In a large mixing bowl, combine whole wheat flour, besan, chopped fenugreek leaves, chilli-ginger paste, sesame seeds, grated jaggery, turmeric, crushed coriander seeds, ajwain, and salt.
Rub the greens and spices into the dry flour with your fingers, then add the curd and 8g of oil and mix.
Gradually sprinkle small amounts of water and knead firmly into a smooth, soft, and slightly tacky dough; rest for ten minutes.
Divide the dough into four equal balls.
Roll each ball out thinly into a uniform circular flatbread using dry flour for dusting.
Place the thepla on a hot tawa, cook one side until small bubbles form, flip and drizzle a little oil; cook both sides until golden spots appear.

name: Millet upma
instructions: Rinse the barnyard millet thoroughly under running water and drain completely.
Heat the ghee in a saucepan and fry the cashews until light golden, then push to one side.
Add mustard seeds and let them crackle, then add urad dal and chana dal and saute until light golden.
Add curry leaves, grated ginger, chopped green chilli, and chopped onion; saute until the onion turns translucent.
Add the drained barnyard millet and stir for a minute.
Pour in two and a half cups of water, add salt, and bring to a rolling boil.
Turn the heat to low, cover the pan, and simmer for twelve to fifteen minutes until the water is absorbed and the millet is fluffy.
Remove from heat, let it sit covered for two minutes, then fluff and serve.

name: Mooli paratha
instructions: Grate the radish finely using a grater and place it in a large bowl, sprinkle a pinch of salt and let it rest for ten minutes.
Squeeze the grated radish firmly between your palms to extract and discard the excess water completely.
Mix the squeezed radish with finely chopped green chilli, coriander leaves, ajwain, and the remaining salt to make the filling.
Knead whole wheat flour with water into a pliable dough.
Divide the dough and the radish filling into two equal portions.
Take one dough ball, flatten it, place the radish filling in the center, and pleat the edges to seal completely.
Dust with flour and roll carefully into a round paratha without tearing.
Cook on a hot tawa, drizzling oil around the edges, until both sides are evenly golden brown.

name: Moong Dal Khichdi
instructions: Wash the sona masoori rice and moong dal together thoroughly. Soak in water for 20 minutes, then drain.
Heat ghee in a pressure cooker over medium heat.
Add cumin seeds and let them splutter, then add asafoetida and turmeric powder.
Add the drained rice and dal mixture to the cooker and sauté for 1-2 minutes to coat with the ghee.
Pour in 3.5 cups of water and add salt. Stir well.
Close the pressure cooker lid and cook for 4 whistles on medium heat.
Allow the pressure to release naturally before opening.
Open the lid and gently stir the soft, mushy khichdi. Serve hot with a drizzle of extra ghee and Gujarati kadhi.

name: Moong dal khichuri
instructions: Dry-roast the moong dal in a pan over medium heat until it turns golden and aromatic.
Wash the roasted dal with the basmati rice together; drain completely.
Heat ghee in a deep pot and add the cumin, bay leaf, green cardamom, cloves, cinnamon and dried red chilli; let them sizzle.
Add grated ginger and slit green chilli; sauté for thirty seconds.
Add the potato halves and toss in the tempered ghee for one minute.
Add the washed rice and dal along with turmeric and salt; stir to coat in the ghee.
Pour in about four katori of hot water, bring to a rolling boil, then lower the flame.
Cover and simmer for twenty minutes until the rice, dal and potato are soft and porridge-like; serve hot with a drizzle of extra ghee.

name: Onion poha
instructions: Place the flattened rice in a colander, rinse it gently under running water, drain completely, and set aside to soften.
Heat groundnut oil in a pan, add mustard seeds, and let them crackle.
Add curry leaves and diced potato, cover, and cook on low heat until the potato is tender.
Add chopped onion and green chilli; saute until onion turns translucent.
Add turmeric powder, salt, and sugar; stir for thirty seconds.
Add the softened flattened rice to the pan and toss gently to coat everything evenly without mashing.
Cover and steam on low heat for two to three minutes.
Turn off the heat, finish with lemon juice and fresh coriander leaves, mix gently, and serve.

name: Onion uttapam
instructions: Soak the rice in one bowl and urad dal with fenugreek seeds in another for five hours, then grind and ferment to a thick uttapam batter for eight to ten hours.
Stir salt into the fermented batter gently.
Finely chop the onion, green chillies, and coriander leaves and mix them together in a bowl.
Heat a cast-iron or non-stick griddle over medium heat and grease lightly with oil.
Pour a thick ladleful of batter onto the tawa, spreading it only slightly to keep it thick like a pancake.
Immediately sprinkle a generous handful of the onion-chilli-coriander mixture evenly over the wet batter and press gently with a spatula.
Drizzle a little oil around the edges, cover the pan, and cook on medium heat until the base is golden and the toppings have softened.
Flip carefully, cook the topping side for a minute until the onions caramelize lightly, then remove and serve.

name: Palak Paneer
instructions: Blanch the spinach leaves in boiling water for 2-3 minutes, then immediately transfer them to ice-cold water to retain their bright green color.
Blend the blanched spinach along with the green chilli into a smooth puree.
Heat butter in a pan over medium heat. Add cumin seeds and let them sizzle.
Add the minced garlic and grated ginger, sautéing until fragrant.
Add the finely chopped onions and cook until they turn translucent and lightly golden.
Stir in the finely chopped tomatoes and salt. Cook until tomatoes are completely soft.
Pour the spinach puree into the pan and mix well. Simmer for 3-5 minutes.
Add the paneer cubes and garam masala. Gently stir to coat the paneer in the sauce.
Simmer for another 2 minutes. Do not overcook or the spinach will lose its color.
Turn off the heat, stir in the fresh cream, and serve hot with naan or roti.

name: Palak paratha
instructions: Wash the spinach leaves thoroughly, blanch them in boiling water for two minutes, then drain and cool quickly under cold water.
Puree the blanched spinach leaves along with the green chilli and ginger in a blender until smooth.
Finely chop the onion.
In a large bowl, combine whole wheat flour, chopped onion, cumin, salt, and the spinach puree.
Knead the mixture into a soft, smooth dough, adding a little water only if needed.
Divide the dough into two equal portions and roll each into a smooth ball.
Roll out each ball into a circular flatbread of even thickness using dry flour for dusting.
Cook the paratha on a hot tawa, drizzling oil around the edges, until both sides are evenly cooked with green-brown patches.

name: Panchmel Dal
instructions: Mix all five dals together, wash them thoroughly, and soak them in water for at least 30 minutes.
Pressure cook the soaked dals with 3 cups of water, turmeric powder, and salt for 4-5 whistles until completely soft. Whisk lightly.
Heat ghee in a heavy pan. Add cumin seeds, cloves, and dried red chillies. Let them sizzle.
Add asafoetida, followed by the minced ginger and garlic. Saute for a minute until aromatic.
Stir in the finely chopped onions and cook until they turn golden brown.
Add the finely chopped tomatoes and red chilli powder. Cook until the tomatoes become mushy and the ghee separates.
Pour the cooked dal into the tempering. Add a little warm water if the dal is too thick.
Simmer on low heat for 5-7 minutes to allow the flavors to blend. Serve hot with Baati or rice.

name: Paneer Bhurji

ingredients.notes: crumbled - reduced from 200g to stay within 80g/serving limit

instructions: Crumble the fresh paneer with your hands and keep it aside.
Heat sunflower oil in a pan over medium heat.
Add cumin seeds and let them splutter.
Add finely chopped onion, ginger, and green chilli. Sauté until the onions are translucent and light pink.
Add the finely chopped tomatoes along with turmeric powder, red chilli powder, and salt.
Cook until the tomatoes turn soft and mushy, and the oil starts to release from the sides.
Add the crumbled paneer into the pan and mix well with the onion-tomato masala.
Cook for just 2-3 minutes. Do not overcook, as the paneer will turn hard and rubbery.
Turn off the heat, garnish with fresh coriander leaves, and serve immediately with hot rotis or bread.

name: Paneer Butter Masala
instructions: In a pan, boil the chopped onions, tomatoes, ginger, garlic, and soaked cashews in half a cup of water for 10-15 minutes until very soft.
Let the mixture cool completely, then blend it into a smooth, fine puree.
Heat butter in a kadai over medium-low heat.
Add the red chilli powder directly to the butter and sauté for a few seconds to release the color (be careful not to burn it).
Immediately pour in the blended onion-tomato puree and stir well.
Cook the gravy for 8-10 minutes until it thickens and starts leaving the sides of the pan.
Add salt, sugar, and garam masala, mixing thoroughly.
Add about half a cup of water to adjust the consistency and bring to a simmer.
Gently fold in the paneer cubes and crushed kasuri methi.
Simmer for 3-4 minutes, then turn off the heat and stir in the fresh cream.
Serve hot with naan, roti, or jeera rice.

name: Papad Ki Sabzi

ingredients.notes: raw papads, typically moong or urad based
use less salt as papad already contains salt

instructions: Roast the raw papads over an open flame or on a tawa until they have small brown spots and turn crisp. Break them into medium-sized pieces and set aside.
In a small bowl, mix the whisked curd with turmeric powder, red chilli powder, and coriander powder to make a spice paste.
Heat ghee in a pan over medium heat. Add cumin seeds and let them splutter.
Add the grated ginger and slit green chilli. Saute for a few seconds.
Lower the flame completely. Pour the spiced curd mixture into the pan and stir continuously and vigorously until it comes to a boil to prevent curdling.
Add 1 cup of water and salt. Let the gravy simmer for 4-5 minutes.
Just before serving, drop the broken roasted papad pieces and crushed kasuri methi into the boiling gravy.
Turn off the heat immediately. Do not overcook as the papad will become soggy quickly.
Garnish with chopped coriander leaves and serve immediately with hot phulkas.

name: Phulka Roti
instructions: In a large bowl, mix the whole wheat flour and salt.
Gradually add water (about 3/4 cup) and knead into a soft, smooth dough. Cover and let it rest for 10 minutes.
Divide the dough into 8 equal-sized portions and roll them into smooth balls.
Take a dough ball, flatten it slightly, dust it with dry flour, and roll it out into a thin 6-inch circle.
Heat a tawa (griddle) over medium-high heat. Place the rolled roti on the hot tawa.
Cook for a few seconds until small bubbles appear, then flip.
Cook the second side for a few more seconds until brown spots appear.
Using tongs, lift the roti off the tawa and place it directly over an open flame, flipping quickly until it puffs up.
Remove from the heat and lightly smear with ghee.
Keep the rotis wrapped in a clean cloth to stay soft, and repeat for the rest of the dough.

name: Poha upma
instructions: Place the flattened rice in a colander, rinse briefly under water, drain thoroughly, and set aside to soften.
Heat ghee in a pan and add mustard seeds; let them crackle.
Add urad dal and chana dal and saute until lightly golden.
Add curry leaves, chopped green chilli, and chopped onion; saute until the onion softens.
Stir in turmeric powder and salt.
Gently fluff the softened flattened rice with your fingers and add it to the pan, tossing carefully to combine without mashing.
Cover the pan and heat through on low flame for two to three minutes.
Remove the lid, stir gently, and serve immediately.

name: Pomfret Fish Curry

ingredients.notes: soaked in 1 cup warm water to extract juice

instructions: Extract the juice from the soaked tamarind, discard the pulp, and keep the tangy water ready.
Heat sesame oil in a wide clay pot or heavy pan over medium heat.
Add mustard seeds and fenugreek seeds. Wait for the mustard to splutter, being careful not to burn the fenugreek.
Add the whole garlic cloves and curry leaves, sautéing until the garlic turns lightly golden.
Add the finely chopped onions and sauté until they are soft and translucent.
Stir in the chopped tomatoes, turmeric powder, red chilli powder, coriander powder, and salt. Cook until tomatoes are mushy and oil separates.
Pour in the tamarind extract and an additional 1 cup of water. Bring the curry base to a rolling boil.
Gently slide the cleaned pomfret fish slices into the boiling curry. Lower the heat to a simmer.
Cover and cook for 8-10 minutes. Do not stir vigorously, or the fish will break. Swirl the pan instead to mix. Serve hot with steamed rice.

name: Potato Roast
instructions: Parboil the cubed potatoes in salted water for 5 minutes until they are half cooked. Drain well.
Heat sesame oil in a wide, heavy-bottomed pan.
Add mustard seeds and let them splutter. Add urad dal, crushed fennel seeds, and crushed garlic.
Sauté for a minute until the garlic smells aromatic and dal turns golden.
Add the curry leaves, followed by the parboiled potato cubes.
Sprinkle turmeric powder, red chilli powder, and salt over the potatoes. Toss well to coat.
Cook uncovered on medium-low heat for 10-15 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Allow the potatoes to roast and form a crispy crust on the outside.
Once fully cooked and crispy, remove from heat and serve hot with sambar or rasam rice.

name: Puliyogare

ingredients.notes: large lemon sized, soaked in hot water and extracted thick

instructions: In a heavy bottom pan, heat sesame oil. Add peanuts and fry until golden. Remove and set aside.
In the same oil, add mustard seeds. When they pop, add chana dal, urad dal, and dried red chillies.
Sauté until the dals are light brown. Add curry leaves and asafoetida.
Carefully pour in the thick tamarind extract, standing back as it might splatter.
Add salt, jaggery, and bring the mixture to a boil.
Reduce heat and let it simmer until the mixture thickens into a paste and oil separates from the edges (about 15-20 minutes).
Add the roasted fenugreek powder and mix well. Turn off the heat.
Add the cooked, cooled rice and fried peanuts to the tamarind paste (pulikachal).
Mix gently until the rice grains are evenly coated. Let it rest for at least 30 minutes before serving.

name: Punjabi Kadhi Pakora
instructions: In a large bowl, whisk sour curd with 30g besan, turmeric powder, half the red chilli powder, and half the salt until smooth. Add 3-4 cups of water and mix well.
Pour the kadhi mixture into a heavy pot and bring it to a boil on medium heat, stirring continuously to prevent curdling.
Once boiling, lower the heat and let it simmer for 25-30 minutes, stirring occasionally until the raw taste of besan goes away.
To make pakoras, combine the remaining 60g besan with sliced onions, chopped green chilli, a pinch of salt, and a little water to make a thick dropping consistency batter.
Heat mustard oil in a small kadai until smoking. Drop small spoonfuls of the batter into the hot oil and fry until golden brown and crisp. Remove and drain.
Gently slide the fried pakoras into the simmering kadhi. Simmer for 5 more minutes so the pakoras soften slightly.
For the tempering, heat ghee in a small pan. Add mustard seeds, cumin seeds, and fenugreek seeds.
When they splutter, add the dried red chillies and the remaining red chilli powder. Immediately turn off the heat to avoid burning.
Pour the hot tempering over the kadhi pakora. Serve steaming hot with jeera rice.
name_alt: Gram Flour Dumplings in Yogurt Curry

name: Rajma Masala
instructions: Drain the soaked rajma, rinse well, and pressure cook with 3 cups of water and half the salt for 5-6 whistles until completely soft and easily mashable.
In a heavy-bottomed pan, heat the sunflower oil. Add the bay leaf and cumin seeds.
Once cumin splutters, add the finely chopped onions. Sauté patiently on medium heat until they turn a deep golden brown.
Add the ginger and garlic paste. Cook for 1-2 minutes until the raw smell disappears.
Pour in the tomato puree, along with turmeric, red chilli powder, and the remaining salt.
Cook the masala until it thickens, leaves the sides of the pan, and the oil separates on top.
Add the boiled rajma along with its cooking liquid to the pan. Mix well.
Simmer on low heat for 15-20 minutes, lightly mashing a few rajma beans against the side of the pan to thicken the gravy.
Sprinkle garam masala and stir well. Garnish with chopped coriander leaves.
Serve hot with steamed basmati rice (Rajma Chawal).

name: Rava upma
instructions: Roast the semolina in a dry pan over medium-low flame until it becomes hot and fragrant, then transfer to a plate.
Heat ghee in the same pan and fry the cashews until light golden, then push to one side.
Add mustard seeds and let them crackle, then add urad dal and chana dal and saute until lightly golden.
Add curry leaves, grated ginger, slit green chilli, and chopped onion; saute until the onion turns translucent.
Pour in three katori of water, add salt, and bring it to a rolling boil.
Lower the heat and gradually add the roasted semolina while stirring constantly to prevent lumps.
Cover the pan and let it simmer for three minutes until all the water is absorbed.
Turn off the heat, fluff the upma gently, and serve hot.

name: Rohu Machher Jhol
instructions: Marinate the rohu fish pieces with half of the turmeric powder and a pinch of salt. Let it rest for 10 minutes.
Heat mustard oil in a heavy pan until it reaches smoking point, then reduce the heat to medium.
Fry the fish pieces until they are golden brown on both sides. Remove and set aside.
In the same oil, fry the potato wedges until lightly golden, then remove and set aside.
Add cumin seeds to the remaining hot oil and allow them to crackle.
Add grated ginger and slit green chillies, sautéing for a few seconds.
Add the chopped tomato, remaining turmeric, red chilli powder, and coriander powder. Cook until the tomatoes become mushy and oil separates.
Pour in 2 cups of water and bring the gravy to a rolling boil.
Add the fried potatoes and salt, cover the pan, and cook for 8-10 minutes until the potatoes are tender.
Gently slide in the fried fish pieces and simmer for 5 minutes so the fish absorbs the flavors.
Turn off the heat and serve the machher jhol hot with steamed white rice.

name: Sada aloo chorchori
instructions: Peel the potatoes and slice into thin matchstick strips; rinse to remove starch and drain.
Heat mustard oil in a non-stick pan until it just begins to smoke, then lower the flame.
Add cumin, fennel and fenugreek seeds along with the broken green chilli; let them crackle.
Add the potato strips and sprinkle turmeric and salt over them; toss to coat evenly.
Stir-fry on medium heat for three to four minutes, allowing the edges to catch slightly.
Add a quarter cup of water, cover the pan, and simmer for eight minutes on low heat.
Uncover and cook off any remaining moisture, stirring gently so the strips do not break.
Remove from heat once the potatoes are tender and lightly glazed, and serve warm with rice.

name: Shukto

ingredients.notes: half for paste, half for tempering

instructions: Grind half of the mustard seeds and the ginger into a fine paste using a little water.
Heat mustard oil in a heavy-bottomed pan until it smokes, then lower the heat.
Fry the bitter gourd pieces until they are crisp and brown. Remove and set aside.
In the same oil, lightly fry the brinjal pieces for 2 minutes, then remove and set aside.
To the remaining hot oil, add the rest of the mustard seeds and let them splutter.
Add the sweet potato, potato, and drumstick pieces. Sauté for 3-4 minutes.
Stir in the prepared mustard-ginger paste and salt, cooking for another 2 minutes.
Add 1.5 cups of water, cover the pan, and simmer until the vegetables are almost tender.
Return the fried bitter gourd and brinjal to the pan, add milk and sugar, and stir gently.
Simmer for 3-4 minutes until the gravy thickens slightly.
Turn off the heat, drizzle ghee on top, and serve as the traditional first course of a Bengali meal with rice.

name: Simple Dosa
instructions: Wash and soak the parboiled rice in one bowl, and the urad dal along with fenugreek seeds in another bowl, for 6-8 hours.
Drain the water. Grind the urad dal mixture in a blender until extremely smooth and fluffy, adding a little ice water as needed.
Transfer to a large vessel. Next, grind the soaked rice until it reaches a slightly grainy, smooth consistency.
Mix the rice batter into the dal batter, add salt, and mix vigorously with clean hands to aerate.
Cover and leave in a warm place to ferment for 8-10 hours until the batter has risen and is bubbly.
When ready to cook, heat a cast-iron tawa (griddle) on medium-high heat. Stir the batter well.
Pour a ladle full of batter in the center of the tawa and spread it outward in quick circular motions to make a thin crepe.
Drizzle half a teaspoon of sesame oil around the edges. Cook until the bottom turns golden brown and crisp, then fold and serve hot.

name: Sona masoori rice dosa
instructions: Rinse and soak the sona masoori rice in one container; soak the urad dal with fenugreek seeds in another for five hours.
Drain the urad dal and fenugreek and grind them into a perfectly fine, light, and bubbly batter using cold water.
Grind the soaked rice into a smooth paste using small splashes of cold water.
Combine both batters in a large container and mix until completely integrated.
Set the batter aside in a warm spot for eight to ten hours to ferment and rise.
Stir in the salt gently once the batter is fermented.
Heat a non-stick or cast-iron tawa over medium heat, lightly grease it with oil, and pour a ladle of batter in the centre.
Spread the batter in a wide circular motion, drizzle a little oil around the edges, and cook until the underside turns golden and crisp; fold and serve hot.

name: Sona masoori rice idli
instructions: Wash the sona masoori rice and urad dal separately in clean water.
Soak the washed rice in one bowl, and the urad dal with fenugreek seeds together in another bowl, for five hours.
Grind the soaked urad dal and fenugreek seeds with minimal cold water until the batter is thick, fluffy, and smooth.
Grind the soaked sona masoori rice separately with a little water to a slightly grainy consistency.
Combine the rice and dal batters thoroughly in a large deep container, leaving enough room for the batter to rise.
Cover the container and let the mixed batter ferment in a warm place for eight to ten hours until it has risen and smells pleasantly sour.
Add salt to the fermented batter and mix gently without deflating it.
Pour the batter into greased idli moulds and steam in an idli steamer on medium-high heat for twelve minutes until cooked through.

name: South Indian Lemon Rice
instructions: Spread the cooked sona masoori rice on a wide plate. Drizzle a few drops of oil and let it cool completely so the grains don't stick.
Heat the sunflower oil in a pan over medium heat. Add the raw peanuts and fry until they are crunchy and lightly browned. Remove peanuts and set aside.
In the same oil, add the mustard seeds. Once they pop, add the chana dal and urad dal. Roast until golden.
Add the slit green chillies, finely chopped ginger, curry leaves, and asafoetida. Sauté for a few seconds until fragrant.
Lower the heat and add the turmeric powder, mixing quickly to avoid burning.
Turn off the heat. Add the cooled rice, salt, and the fried peanuts to the pan.
Pour the freshly squeezed lemon juice over the rice.
Mix everything gently but thoroughly until the rice takes on a uniform, vibrant yellow color. Serve warm or at room temperature.

name: South Indian Potato Sagu

ingredients.notes: mixed with 1/4 cup water to form a slurry

instructions: Heat the sunflower oil in a pan over medium heat. Add the mustard seeds and let them splutter.
Add the raw chana dal and urad dal, roasting them until they turn golden brown and nutty.
Stir in the slit green chillies, grated ginger, and curry leaves. Sauté for 30 seconds.
Add the thinly sliced onions and cook until they turn translucent and soft, but do not brown them.
Add the turmeric powder and salt, mixing well. Then add the roughly mashed boiled potatoes.
Pour in about 1 cup of water and mix. Bring the mixture to a gentle boil.
Slowly pour in the besan-water slurry while stirring continuously. This will thicken the sagu and give it a creamy texture.
Simmer for 3-4 minutes until the raw smell of besan is gone. Turn off the heat, stir in lemon juice, garnish with coriander leaves, and serve hot with chapati or dosa.

name: South Indian Sambar
instructions: Pressure cook the toor dal with turmeric powder and 2 cups of water for 4 whistles until completely mushy.
Mash the cooked dal well and set aside.
In a large pot, heat sesame oil over medium heat.
Add mustard seeds and let them splutter. Then add fenugreek seeds, asafoetida, and curry leaves.
Add the sliced onions and sauté until they turn translucent.
Add the chopped tomatoes and drumstick pieces, sautéing for 2 minutes.
Pour in the tamarind extract along with coriander powder, red chilli powder, and salt. Add 1 cup of water.
Cover and boil for 10-12 minutes until the raw smell of tamarind goes away and drumsticks are tender.
Stir in the mashed toor dal. Adjust consistency by adding water if it is too thick.
Simmer for another 5 minutes to let the flavors blend together.
Turn off the heat and serve hot with steamed rice or idli.

name: South Indian Tomato Rasam

ingredients.notes: soaked in warm water to extract juice

instructions: In a mortar and pestle, coarsely crush the black pepper and half of the cumin. Set aside.
In a pot, add the chopped tomatoes, tamarind extract, crushed garlic, turmeric powder, salt, and 2.5 cups of water.
Bring this mixture to a gentle boil and simmer for 10 minutes until the tomatoes are completely soft and mushy.
Stir in the coarsely crushed black pepper and cumin mixture. Simmer for just 2 more minutes until frothy, then turn off the heat.
In a small pan, heat the sunflower oil. Add mustard seeds, remaining cumin, dried red chilli, curry leaves, and asafoetida. Let them splutter.
Pour the hot tempering over the rasam, garnish generously with fresh coriander leaves, and serve hot as a soup or over rice.

name: Spicy Andhra Chicken Curry
instructions: Marinate the chicken pieces with turmeric powder, half the salt, and a teaspoon of ginger-garlic paste for 15 minutes.
Heat the sunflower oil in a heavy-bottomed kadai or pan over medium-high heat.
Add the curry leaves and slit green chillies, letting them crackle for a few seconds to release their heat.
Add the finely chopped onions and sauté patiently until they turn a deep golden brown.
Stir in the remaining ginger and garlic paste, cooking for 2 minutes until the raw smell vanishes.
Add the chopped tomatoes, red chilli powder, and coriander powder. Cook until the oil begins to separate from the masala.
Add the marinated chicken pieces and sauté on high heat for 5-7 minutes to seal the juices.
Pour in 1 cup of hot water, cover the pan, and simmer on medium-low heat for 20 minutes until the chicken is tender and fully cooked.
Stir in the garam masala and remaining salt, simmering for another 3 minutes until the gravy thickens.
Garnish generously with freshly chopped coriander leaves and serve with white rice or parotta.

name: Steamed Sona Masoori Rice
instructions: Wash the sona masoori rice thoroughly under running water until the water runs clear.
Soak the washed rice in freshwater for 15 minutes to ensure softer grains, then drain.
In a heavy-bottomed pot, bring 2.5 cups of water to a boil along with the salt.
Add the drained rice to the boiling water. Stir once, cover with a tight-fitting lid, and lower the heat to the minimum setting.
Cook undisturbed for 15-18 minutes until all the water is absorbed and the grains are tender.
Turn off the heat, let it rest for 5 minutes, then fluff gently. Drizzle with ghee before serving with rasam or sambar.

name: Suji dhokla

ingredients.notes: 5g crushed into batter paste, 5g slit for tempering
dissolved in 3 tbsp warm water for drizzle

instructions: In a deep bowl, whisk the semolina with curd and 60ml water into a smooth, thick yet pourable batter.
Pound the ginger and 5g of the green chilli into a smooth paste and stir into the batter with turmeric, salt, and lemon juice.
Cover the bowl and let the batter rest for fifteen minutes so the semolina absorbs the moisture.
Set up a steamer with water and bring to a boil over medium-high heat.
Stir the rested batter gently, then pour it into a lightly greased shallow steel steaming plate.
Place the plate inside the steamer, cover securely, and steam on high heat for twelve to fifteen minutes until a toothpick comes out clean.
Remove the plate, cool slightly, and cut into squares.

Heat the groundnut oil in a small pan, splutter mustard seeds, add sesame seeds, slit green chilli, and curry leaves; pour the hot tempering over the dhoklas and drizzle the sugar-water syrup evenly on top before serving.

name: Tamil Style Brinjal Curry

ingredients.notes: lemon-sized ball mapped to pulp, soaked in 1.5 cups warm water
finely chopped (pearl onions preferred if available)

instructions: Wash the brinjals and make a cross slit from the base without cutting them fully. Soak in salt water to prevent discoloration.
Mix the tamarind pulp with 1.5 cups warm water to make a thin extract.
Heat 2 tablespoons of sesame oil in a heavy-bottomed pan. Add the slit brinjals and fry them until the skin blisters and they are half cooked. Remove and set aside.
In the same pan, add the remaining 1 tablespoon of sesame oil. Add mustard seeds and fenugreek seeds.
Once the mustard seeds splutter, add the whole garlic cloves and curry leaves, roasting until garlic turns slightly golden.
Add the finely chopped onions and sauté until translucent.
Stir in the chopped tomatoes, turmeric powder, red chilli powder, coriander powder, and salt. Cook until the tomatoes are completely mushy.
Pour the tamarind extract into the pan and bring to a rolling boil.
Gently drop the fried brinjals back into the boiling gravy. Lower the heat, cover, and simmer for 12-15 minutes.
Cook until the gravy thickens considerably, the brinjals are tender, and the sesame oil floats to the top. Serve hot with rice.

name: Tomato Onion Chutney
instructions: Heat half the sesame oil in a pan over medium heat. Add the chana dal and urad dal, roasting until golden.
Add the dried red chillies and garlic cloves, sautéing for a minute.
Toss in the roughly chopped onions and cook until they turn translucent and lightly browned.
Add the chopped tomatoes and salt. Cook until the tomatoes are mushy and have lost their raw smell.
Turn off the heat and allow the mixture to cool completely. Blend it into a smooth paste without adding extra water.
For the tempering, heat the remaining sesame oil in a small pan. Add mustard seeds, let them pop, then add curry leaves and asafoetida. Pour over the blended chutney.

name: Tomato Pappu
instructions: In a pressure cooker, add the washed toor dal, chopped tomatoes, green chillies, turmeric powder, and 2.5 cups of water.
Pressure cook for 4-5 whistles until the dal and tomatoes are extremely soft.
Once pressure releases, add salt and red chilli powder. Mash the dal vigorously using a spoon or traditional wooden masher.
Adjust the consistency by adding a little warm water if necessary.
In a small pan, heat sunflower oil for the tempering (popu).
Add mustard seeds and let them pop. Add cumin seeds, broken dried red chillies, and crushed garlic.
Fry until garlic is light brown, then add the curry leaves and sauté for a couple of seconds.
Pour the hot tempering directly into the mashed dal and mix well.
Simmer for 2 minutes to let flavors meld, then serve hot with rice and ghee.

name: Tomato Rasam
instructions: Extract the juice from the soaked tamarind using 2 cups of water.
In a bowl, combine the chopped tomatoes, tamarind water, turmeric powder, and salt. Hand crush the tomatoes into the liquid.
Using a mortar and pestle, coarsely crush the black pepper, cumin seeds, and garlic cloves.
Heat ghee in a pot over medium heat.
Add mustard seeds and let them pop. Add curry leaves and the freshly crushed pepper-cumin-garlic mixture.
Sauté for 30 seconds until very fragrant.
Pour in the prepared tomato-tamarind water.
Keep the flame on medium and let it cook until a frothy layer forms on top and it is just about to boil.
Do not let the rasam rolling boil, as it alters the flavor. Turn off the heat immediately.
Garnish generously with chopped coriander leaves.
Serve hot as a soup or mixed with rice.

name: Tomato uttapam
instructions: Soak the rice in one bowl and the urad dal with fenugreek seeds in another for five hours, then grind and ferment to a thick uttapam batter for eight to ten hours.
Mix salt into the fermented batter gently.
Finely chop the tomatoes, green chilli, and coriander leaves and combine in a bowl.
Preheat a dosa tawa on medium flame and grease lightly with oil.
Pour a thick ladleful of batter onto the hot tawa without spreading it thin.
Spread a layer of the tomato mixture evenly on top and press lightly with a spatula.
Drizzle a little oil around the edges, cover the pan, and cook until the underside is golden brown.
Flip carefully, cook the topping side for a minute until tomatoes soften and caramelize, then remove and serve.

name: Toor Dal Tadka
instructions: In a pressure cooker, add the washed toor dal, turmeric powder, half the salt, and 2.5 cups of water.
Cook for 3-4 whistles on medium heat until the dal is completely soft and mushy.
Let the pressure release naturally, then whisk the dal lightly to smooth it out. Set aside.
In a separate small pan, heat the ghee over medium heat for the tempering (tadka).
Add the cumin seeds and let them splutter for a few seconds.
Add the minced garlic, grated ginger, and slit green chilli. Sauté for 30 seconds until aromatic.
Add the finely chopped onion and cook until they turn translucent and slightly golden.
Stir in the chopped tomatoes and red chilli powder. Cook for 3-4 minutes until the tomatoes soften.
Pour this hot tempering over the cooked dal and mix well. Simmer for 2 minutes so flavors meld.
Garnish with freshly chopped coriander leaves and serve hot with rice or roti.

name: Vegetable mix paratha
instructions: Boil the potato and carrot until soft, then peel and mash them thoroughly in a bowl.
Finely grate the cauliflower florets and finely chop the onion, green chilli, and coriander leaves.
Combine the mashed potato and carrot, grated cauliflower, chopped onion, green chilli, coriander leaves, cumin, garam masala, and salt to make the vegetable filling.
Knead whole wheat flour with water into a smooth pliable dough.
Divide the dough into two equal parts and shape into neat balls.
Roll a dough ball slightly, place half of the filling inside, and pinch the edges to seal well.
Flatten the stuffed ball and roll it out gently into a round paratha, ensuring the filling does not leak.
Cook on a hot griddle, drizzling oil around the edges, until both sides have golden-brown spots and the paratha is fully cooked.

name: Vegetable rava upma
instructions: Dry-roast the semolina until lightly toasted and fragrant, then set aside on a plate.
Heat the ghee in the same pan and fry the cashews until golden, then push to one side.
Add mustard seeds and let them crackle, then add urad dal and chana dal and saute until lightly golden.
Add curry leaves, grated ginger, chopped green chilli, chopped onion, carrot, and french beans; saute on medium flame until the vegetables are slightly tender.
Pour in three katori of water, add salt, and bring it to a rolling boil.
