Gradually pour in the roasted semolina while stirring quickly to prevent lumps from forming.
Reduce heat to low, cover with a lid, and cook for three to four minutes until the water is absorbed.
Uncover, fluff the upma gently from the bottom of the pan, and serve hot.

name: Vegetable upma
instructions: Dry-roast the semolina in a pan over medium heat until it becomes fragrant and lightly golden, then transfer to a plate.
Heat groundnut oil in the same pan, add mustard seeds and let them crackle.
Add urad dal and chana dal; saute until lightly golden.
Add curry leaves, ginger, green chilli, and chopped onion; saute until onion is translucent.
Add carrots and green peas, stir for a minute, then pour in two and a half cups of water and add salt; bring to a rolling boil.
Lower the heat and slowly add the roasted semolina while stirring continuously to prevent lumps.
Keep stirring as the semolina absorbs the water and thickens to a uniform consistency.
Cover the pan and let the upma steam on low heat for two to three minutes before fluffing and serving.

name: Vegetable uttapam
instructions: Soak the rice in one bowl and the urad dal with fenugreek seeds in another for five hours, then grind and ferment to a thick uttapam batter for eight to ten hours.
Stir salt into the fermented batter gently.
Chop the onion, green chilli, and coriander leaves; grate the carrot finely.
Mix all the chopped and grated vegetables together in a bowl.
Heat a non-stick tawa over medium heat, grease it lightly, and ladle a generous amount of batter to form a thick disc.
Sprinkle the vegetable mixture generously across the top surface and press gently with a spatula to embed them into the batter.
Drizzle oil around the edges, cover the pan, and cook until the base turns golden brown.
Flip carefully, cook the vegetable side for a minute, then remove and serve.

name: Ven pongal
instructions: Dry-roast the moong dal in a pressure cooker on low flame for three minutes until lightly fragrant.
Add the sona masoori rice to the cooker and rinse both rice and dal together with water, then drain.
Add four and a half cups of fresh water and salt to the cooker.
Close the lid and pressure cook for four to five whistles until the rice and dal are completely soft and mushy.
Once the pressure releases, open the cooker and mash the mixture gently with a ladle.
Heat the ghee in a small pan, add the cashew pieces and fry until golden.
Add cumin, coarsely crushed black pepper, chopped ginger, asafoetida, and curry leaves to the ghee and let them splutter.
Pour the entire tempering over the cooked rice-dal mixture, stir to combine, and serve hot.

name: Whole Wheat Phulka
instructions: In a large mixing bowl, combine the whole wheat flour and salt.
Gradually add warm water, mixing continuously, until the dough begins to come together.
Knead the dough for 5-8 minutes until it is smooth, soft, and pliable.
Cover the dough with a damp cloth and let it rest for at least 15 minutes.
Divide the rested dough into equal lemon-sized balls and flatten them slightly.
Dust a dough ball with dry flour and roll it out into a thin, even circle using a rolling pin.
Heat a tawa (griddle) over medium-high heat. Place the rolled dough circle on it.
When small bubbles appear, flip it over and cook the other side for a few more seconds.
Carefully move the roti directly to an open flame using tongs; it will puff up immediately.
Remove from heat, brush lightly with ghee, and keep covered in a cloth to retain softness.

name: Masala Omelette
instructions: In a bowl, crack the eggs and whisk them thoroughly until slightly frothy.
Add the chopped onion, tomato, green chilli, and coriander leaves to the eggs.
Add turmeric powder, red chilli powder, and salt, mixing well to combine all ingredients.
Heat oil in a non-stick pan over medium heat.
Pour half of the egg mixture into the pan, swirling to spread it evenly.
Cook for 2-3 minutes until the bottom is set and slightly golden.
Flip carefully and cook the other side for another 1-2 minutes.
Remove from heat and repeat with the remaining egg mixture.
Serve hot with toast or paratha.

name: Egg Paratha
instructions: Divide the pre-kneaded whole wheat dough into 2 equal portions and roll them into smooth balls.
In a small bowl, beat the eggs with chopped onion, green chilli, and a pinch of salt.
Roll out one dough ball into a thin circle using a rolling pin.
Heat a tawa or flat pan over medium heat and place the rolled dough on it.
Cook for a minute until small bubbles appear, then flip.
Spread half a teaspoon of ghee on the surface, then carefully pour half of the egg mixture over the paratha.
Gently spread the egg mixture with a spoon and wait 30 seconds for it to slightly set.
Flip the paratha quickly to cook the egg side down.
Press gently with a spatula and apply a little more ghee to the edges until the egg is cooked and the paratha is golden brown.
Repeat for the second paratha and serve hot.

name: Egg Bhurji
instructions: Crack the eggs into a bowl, whisk well, and set aside.
Heat oil in a pan over medium heat and add cumin seeds.
Once the seeds crackle, add chopped onions and green chillies, sautéing until onions turn translucent.
Add chopped tomatoes, turmeric powder, red chilli powder, and salt. Cook until tomatoes are soft and oil starts to separate.
Reduce the heat and pour in the beaten eggs.
Stir continuously to scramble the eggs and mix them with the onion-tomato masala.
Cook for 3-4 minutes until the eggs are fully cooked but still slightly soft.
Garnish with freshly chopped coriander leaves.
Serve hot with roti, paratha, or bread.

name: Egg Dosa
instructions: Prepare the dosa batter using fermented idli rava and urad dal, ensuring it has a pourable consistency.
Heat a flat non-stick dosa tawa over medium-high heat and grease lightly with a few drops of sesame oil.
Pour a ladle of batter in the center and spread it outward in a circular motion to make a thin crepe.
Crack one egg directly onto the center of the dosa while it is still cooking.
Quickly spread the egg over the surface of the dosa using the back of a spoon.
Drizzle half a teaspoon of sesame oil around the edges.
Sprinkle a tiny pinch of salt over the egg.
Cook until the egg sets and the bottom of the dosa turns golden brown and crispy.
Fold the dosa in half and remove from heat.
Repeat for the second dosa and serve immediately.

name: Egg Curry Rice Bowl
instructions: Cook the sona masoori rice with enough water until fluffy, then set aside.
Boil the eggs, peel them, and make shallow slits on the egg whites.
Heat coconut oil in a deep pan. Add mustard seeds and wait for them to splutter, then add curry leaves.
Add sliced onions and sauté until golden brown.
Add chopped tomatoes and cook until they soften and turn mushy.
Stir in turmeric powder, red chilli powder, crushed coriander seeds, and half the salt. Mix well.
Add half a cup of water to create a gravy consistency and bring to a simmer.
Gently drop the boiled eggs into the curry and simmer for 5 minutes.
To serve, divide the cooked rice into bowls and pour the hot egg curry over the top.

name: Anda Biryani
instructions: Boil the soaked basmati rice with whole spices (optional) and salt until 80% cooked. Drain and set aside.
Heat half the ghee in a heavy-bottomed pot and fry the boiled eggs slightly until golden. Remove and set aside.
In the same pot, fry thinly sliced onions until crisp and golden brown (birista). Keep half aside for garnish.
Add ginger and garlic paste to the remaining onions and sauté until the raw smell disappears.
Stir in tomatoes, green chillies, turmeric, red chilli powder, and garam masala. Cook until tomatoes are mushy.
Lower the flame, stir in whisked curd, and cook until oil separates. Season with salt.
Place the fried eggs into this masala, then layer the par-cooked rice over it.
Sprinkle the remaining fried onions, coriander leaves, and the rest of the ghee on top.
Cover tightly and cook on Dum (very low heat) for 15-20 minutes.
Gently fluff the biryani before serving hot.

name: Egg Fried Rice
instructions: Crack eggs into a bowl, whisk slightly, and scramble them in a heated pan with a few drops of oil. Set scrambled eggs aside.
In a wok or large pan, heat the remaining oil on high heat.
Add minced garlic and stir-fry for a few seconds until fragrant.
Add carrots and french beans, tossing continuously for 2-3 minutes.
Add chopped capsicum and cook for another minute, keeping the vegetables crunchy.
Add the cooked, cooled rice to the wok along with scrambled eggs.
Sprinkle salt and crushed black pepper.
Toss everything together on high heat for 2-3 minutes until the rice is heated through.
Serve hot immediately.

name: Egg White Bhurji Bowl
instructions: Separate the egg whites from the yolks and whisk the egg whites slightly in a bowl.
Heat a minimal amount of oil in a non-stick pan over medium heat.
Add chopped onions and green chilli, sautéing until onions are soft.
Stir in chopped tomatoes and turmeric powder, cooking for 2 minutes.
Pour in the egg whites and continuously stir to scramble them.
Add salt and cook for a few more minutes until the egg whites are fully cooked but not rubbery.
Transfer to a bowl and serve warm.

name: Egg Drop Rasam
instructions: In a bowl, mix tamarind pulp and mashed tomato with 2 cups of water.
Heat sesame oil in a pot, add mustard seeds and let them crackle.
Add curry leaves and the freshly crushed mixture of garlic, cumin, and black pepper. Sauté for 1 minute.
Pour in the tamarind-tomato water and add salt. Bring to a gentle boil.
Reduce the heat to a simmer. Crack the eggs directly into the simmering rasam.
Do not stir immediately; let the eggs poach in the hot liquid for 3-4 minutes until set.
Gently stir to ensure the rasam flavors meld. Garnish with coriander leaves.
Serve hot as a soup or with rice.

name: Masala Egg Curry
instructions: In a pan, dry roast sesame seeds and peanuts until fragrant, then grind into a fine paste with a little water.
Heat a little oil and sauté sliced onions, ginger, and garlic until golden. Cool and blend into a smooth paste.
Heat the remaining oil in a heavy-bottomed pan, add the onion paste, and cook until oil separates.
Add chopped tomatoes, turmeric, red chilli powder, and garam masala. Cook until tomatoes are completely soft.
Stir in the peanut-sesame paste and cook for 3-4 minutes.
Add 1.5 cups of water and salt, bringing the curry to a boil, then simmering until it reaches desired thickness.
Make small incisions on the boiled eggs and drop them into the simmering gravy.
Cook for another 5 minutes, garnish with coriander leaves, and serve with bhakri or rice.

name: Masala Egg Salad
instructions: Peel the hard-boiled eggs and cut them into quarters or chunks.
In a large mixing bowl, combine the chopped onion, tomato, capsicum, and grated carrot.
Add lemon juice, black pepper, and salt to the vegetables and toss gently to coat.
Add the boiled egg chunks to the bowl.
Gently mix everything together, being careful not to mash the egg yolks entirely.
Garnish with freshly chopped coriander leaves.
Serve immediately as a light dinner or side dish.

name: Chicken Keema Paratha
instructions: Knead whole wheat flour with water and a pinch of salt into a soft dough, then cover and rest.
Heat half the oil in a pan, add chopped onion, green chilli, and ginger, cooking until onions soften.
Add minced chicken breast, salt, red chilli powder, and garam masala to the pan.
Cook the chicken mix thoroughly for 8-10 minutes until completely dry, then mix in fresh coriander leaves and let cool.
Divide the rested dough into two equal portions and roll each into a small disc.
Place half of the cooled chicken stuffing in the center of a dough disc, pleat the edges to seal, and flatten.
Roll out the stuffed dough gently into a thick paratha using dry flour to avoid tearing.
Cook on a hot tawa on both sides, applying the remaining oil until golden brown spots appear.
Repeat the rolling and cooking process for the second portion and serve hot.

name: Chicken Poha
instructions: Rinse poha in a colander under running water for a few seconds, drain completely, and set aside to soften.
Heat groundnut oil in a pan, add mustard seeds, and let them splutter.
Add the chopped onion, green chilli, and curry leaves to the pan, sautéing until onions turn translucent.
Add the finely minced chicken breast, turmeric powder, and half the salt.
Sauté the chicken on medium heat for 6-8 minutes until it is completely cooked and slightly browned.
Fluff the softened poha gently with a fork and add it to the pan along with the remaining salt.
Mix everything thoroughly but gently to avoid breaking the flattened rice grains.
Cover the pan with a lid and steam on low heat for 2-3 minutes.
Turn off the heat, stir in lemon juice and fresh coriander leaves, then serve hot.

name: Chicken Curry with Rice
instructions: Wash and soak the basmati rice in water for 20 minutes, then drain.
Boil the soaked rice in water with a pinch of salt until fully cooked, drain excess water, and set aside.
Heat sunflower oil in a separate pan, add chopped onions, and sauté until golden brown.
Add ginger paste and garlic paste, frying for another minute until fragrant.
Stir in the tomato puree, turmeric powder, red chilli powder, and salt, cooking until the oil begins to separate.
Add the diced chicken thigh pieces and stir well to coat them thoroughly with the masala base.
Pour in one cup of water, cover the pan, and simmer on low heat for 15 minutes until the chicken is tender.
Sprinkle garam masala and simmer for another 2 minutes, then garnish with fresh coriander leaves.
Serve the chicken curry hot alongside the cooked basmati rice.

name: Chicken Biryani
instructions: Marinate the chicken pieces with curd, turmeric powder, red chilli powder, and half the salt for 30 minutes.
Wash the basmati rice and soak it in water for 20 minutes, then drain completely.
Parboil the soaked rice in plenty of salted water with cloves and cinnamon until it is 70% cooked, then drain.
Heat ghee in a large heavy-bottomed pot, add the sliced onions, and fry until golden brown.
Add the ginger and garlic pastes along with slit green chillies, sautéing for 2 minutes.
Add the chopped tomatoes and cook until they soften completely.
Add the marinated chicken pieces to the pot and cook on high heat for 5 minutes until sealed.
Reduce heat, cover, and let the chicken cook in its own juices for 10 minutes.
Layer the parboiled rice evenly over the chicken base, scatter fresh coriander leaves on top, cover tightly, and cook on very low heat (Dum) for 15 minutes before serving.

name: Butter Chicken Lite
instructions: Marinate chicken breast cubes with curd, ginger paste, garlic paste, and half the salt for 20 minutes.
Heat a non-stick pan over medium heat, add the marinated chicken, and cook until golden and tender, then remove.
In the same pan, melt the butter, then add the pureed tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes.
Stir the ground cashew paste into the tomatoes and simmer until the mixture thickens slightly.
Add the remaining salt, garam masala, and a splash of water to form a smooth gravy.
Return the cooked chicken pieces to the gravy and simmer together for 5 minutes.
Stir in the fresh cream and crushed kasuri methi, blending well on low heat.
Remove from heat and serve hot.

name: Chicken Tikka Salad
instructions: Marinate the chicken strips in curd, red chilli powder, garam masala, and half the salt for 15 minutes.
Heat the sunflower oil in a non-stick pan over medium-high heat.
Add the marinated chicken strips and pan-sear them for 6-8 minutes until cooked through and lightly charred.
In a large mixing bowl, combine the sliced onions, capsicum, and deseeded tomatoes.
Transfer the hot chicken tikka pieces into the bowl with the fresh vegetables.
Toss the mixture together with the remaining salt and lemon juice.
Serve immediately as a light, high-protein meal.

name: Chicken Fried Rice
instructions: Cook the Sona Masoori rice in advance, drain thoroughly, fluff, and ensure it is completely cold before using.
Heat half the sunflower oil in a wok or deep pan over high heat, add the chicken pieces, and stir-fry until cooked and white throughout, then remove.
Add the remaining oil to the same wok on high heat and toss in the chopped garlic and onions, stir-frying for 1 minute.
Add the finely chopped carrots and french beans, stir-frying rapidly for 2-3 minutes so they stay crisp.
Return the cooked chicken back to the wok alongside the vegetables.
Add the cold cooked rice, spreading it evenly across the wok.
Season everything with salt and freshly crushed black pepper.
Toss the fried rice continuously on high heat for 2 minutes until everything is evenly incorporated and heated through.

name: Chicken Chettinad
instructions: Dry roast coriander seeds, cumin, fennel seeds, and dried red chillies in a pan until fragrant, then grind with a little water into a smooth masala paste.
Heat sesame oil in a pot, add the fresh curry leaves, and let them crackle.
Add the chopped onions and sauté until dark golden brown.
Stir in the ginger paste and garlic paste, frying for 1 minute to remove the raw smell.
Add the chopped tomatoes and turmeric powder, cooking until the tomatoes mash completely.
Add the prepared Chettinad masala paste and salt, stir-frying for 2 minutes over medium heat.
Add the chicken thigh pieces and toss thoroughly to coat them in the rich spice mixture.
Pour in half a cup of water, cover the pot, and cook on medium-low heat for 18-20 minutes until the chicken is tender and the gravy is thick.

name: Grilled Chicken and Veggie Bowl
instructions: Marinate the chicken breast fillets with minced garlic, lemon juice, half the crushed black pepper, and half the salt for 15 minutes.
Steam the sliced carrots and cauliflower florets for 4-5 minutes until tender-crisp, then set aside.
Heat half the sunflower oil in a grill pan or non-stick skillet over medium-high heat.
Place the marinated chicken breast fillets in the pan and grill for 5-6 minutes on each side until fully cooked.
Remove the cooked chicken from the pan, let it rest briefly, and slice into strips.
Add the remaining oil to the same pan and toss in the diced capsicum along with the steamed carrots and cauliflower.
Sauté the vegetables on high heat for 2 minutes, seasoning with the remaining salt and black pepper.
Assemble the meal bowls by placing the sautéed vegetables on one side and the grilled chicken strips on the other.

name: Chicken Saagwala
instructions: Blanch the fresh spinach leaves in boiling water for 2 minutes, plunge them into cold water, and puree smoothly.
Heat sunflower oil in a pan, add the cumin seeds, and let them sizzle.
Add the finely chopped onions and sauté until translucent.
Incorporate the ginger paste and garlic paste, frying for an additional minute.
Add the chopped tomatoes and cook until they soften completely.
Add the chicken thigh cubes and sauté for 5 minutes until the meat turns opaque.
Pour in the spinach puree and add the salt, mixing thoroughly.
Cover the pan and simmer on low heat for 10-12 minutes until the chicken is thoroughly cooked.
Stir in the garam masala just before turning off the heat, mixing gently.

name: Chicken Shorba
instructions: Heat sunflower oil in a deep pot, add the chopped onions, and sauté until they turn light brown.
Add the ginger paste and garlic paste, sautéing briefly for 30 seconds.
Add the small chicken breast cubes along with turmeric powder, cumin powder, and half the black pepper.
Sauté the chicken pieces for 3-4 minutes until they turn white exteriorly.
Pour in 2.5 cups of water and add the salt, stirring well to combine.
Bring the soup to a boil, then reduce the heat, cover with a lid, and simmer for 12-15 minutes.
Stir in the remaining black pepper powder and check the seasoning.
Garnish with fresh chopped coriander leaves and serve warm as a soothing broth.

name: Tandoori Chicken
instructions: Make shallow cuts across the chicken thigh chunks to help the marinade penetrate.
In a bowl, mix thick curd, mustard oil, ginger paste, garlic paste, red chilli powder, garam masala, crushed kasuri methi, salt, and lemon juice into a smooth paste.
Rub the marinade thoroughly into the chicken pieces and set aside to rest for at least 30 minutes.
Preheat your oven to 220°C (or heat a non-stick grill pan over high heat).
Place the marinated chicken chunks on a wire rack or directly onto the hot pan.
Roast or pan-grill for 10-12 minutes on one side until slightly charred.
Flip the chicken pieces over and cook the other side for another 10 minutes until completely cooked and edges are smoky.
Remove from heat, let it rest for 2 minutes, and serve hot.

name: Mutton Keema
instructions: Heat sunflower oil in a thick-bottomed pan or kadhai.
Add cumin seeds and let them splutter.
Add chopped onions and sauté until golden brown.
Add minced ginger, garlic, and green chillies, sautéing for another 2 minutes.
Mix in tomatoes, coriander powder, red chilli powder, turmeric, and salt. Cook until oil separates.
Add the minced mutton (keema) and roast it on medium-high heat for 10-15 minutes until it changes color completely.
Add green peas and a splash of water. Cover and simmer for 15-20 minutes until mutton and peas are fully cooked.
Sprinkle garam masala and mix well.
Garnish with fresh coriander leaves and serve hot.

name: Mutton Rogan Josh
instructions: Heat mustard oil in a heavy-bottomed pot until it smokes, then reduce heat.
Add black cardamom, green cardamom, cloves, and cinnamon. Sauté for 30 seconds.
Add sliced onions and fry until they turn deep golden brown.
Add ginger and garlic paste, and sauté for 2 minutes.
Add mutton pieces and roast on high heat for 10 minutes until well browned.
Lower the heat and add red chilli powder and salt. Mix thoroughly.
Gradually stir in the whisked curd, ensuring it does not curdle.
Add fennel powder and 2 cups of water. Bring to a boil.
Cover tightly and simmer on low heat for 45-60 minutes until mutton is tender and oil floats on top.
Serve hot with steamed rice or flatbreads.

name: Mutton Curry
instructions: Heat oil in a pressure cooker or deep pot.
Add bay leaf and cumin seeds; let them splutter.
Add chopped onions and fry until golden brown.
Stir in ginger and garlic paste, sautéing until the raw smell disappears.
Add tomatoes, turmeric, coriander powder, red chilli powder, and salt. Cook until oil separates.
Add the mutton pieces and sear on medium-high heat for 8-10 minutes.
Add potato chunks and pour in 1.5 cups of water.
If using a pressure cooker, cook for 4-5 whistles. If using a pot, cover and simmer for 50-60 minutes until meat is tender.
Sprinkle garam masala and garnish with fresh coriander leaves.
Serve hot with rice or roti.

name: Prawn Masala
instructions: Marinate prawns with turmeric and a pinch of salt for 10 minutes.
Heat coconut oil in a pan; add mustard seeds and let them pop.
Add curry leaves, green chilli, and chopped onions. Sauté until onions are soft.
Mix in ginger and garlic, sautéing for another minute.
Add tomatoes, red chilli powder, coriander powder, and remaining salt. Cook until tomatoes turn mushy.
Add tamarind pulp and 1/4 cup of water, bringing the masala to a simmer.
Gently fold in the marinated prawns.
Cook for 5-7 minutes until the prawns are opaque and cooked through.
Serve hot with steamed rice or bread.

name: Fish Fry (Tawa)
instructions: Make slits on the pomfret pieces to allow the marinade to seep in.
In a small bowl, mix lemon juice, ginger paste, garlic paste, red chilli powder, turmeric, and salt to form a thick paste.
Rub the marinade evenly over the fish and inside the slits.
Let the fish marinate for 15-20 minutes.
Heat coconut oil in a shallow frying pan or tawa.
Place the marinated fish on the tawa and fry on medium heat for 4-5 minutes per side until crisp and cooked through.
Drain excess oil and serve hot with onion rings and lemon wedges.

name: Prawn Curry
instructions: Heat coconut oil in an earthen pot or heavy pan.
Add mustard seeds and fenugreek seeds; allow them to splutter.
Add curry leaves and chopped onions, frying until onions are translucent.
Stir in crushed ginger and garlic, cooking until fragrant.
Add tomatoes, turmeric, red chilli powder, and coriander powder. Sauté until tomatoes break down.
Pour in the tamarind extract along with 1 cup of water and salt. Bring to a rolling boil.
Add the cleaned prawns, reduce the heat, and simmer gently for 6-8 minutes.
Once the oil surfaces and prawns are cooked, turn off the heat.
Let the curry rest for 15 minutes before serving with rice.

name: Tandoori Fish Tikka Salad
instructions: In a mixing bowl, combine thick curd, ginger paste, garlic paste, lemon juice, garam masala, red chilli powder, turmeric, and half of the salt.
Add mustard oil to the marinade and whisk well.
Add the boneless rohu fish pieces to the marinade, coating them evenly. Rest for 15-20 minutes.
Preheat an oven, air fryer, or heavy pan. Cook the fish tikka for 10-12 minutes until perfectly charred and fully cooked.
While the fish cooks, toss sliced onion, tomato, capsicum, carrot, and cabbage in a large salad bowl.
Add the remaining salt, a squeeze of lemon if desired, and fresh coriander leaves to the vegetables.
Arrange the hot fish tikkas over the mixed salad.
Serve immediately as a healthy, high-protein dinner.

name: Paneer Dosa
instructions: Wash and soak idli rava, urad dal, and fenugreek seeds in water for 6-8 hours.
Grind the soaked mixture into a smooth batter adding a little water.
Add salt to the batter, mix well, and let it ferment overnight.
Heat a non-stick pan or tawa and pour a ladleful of batter, spreading it thinly in a circular motion.
Drizzle ghee around the edges and cook until the bottom turns golden crisp.
Sprinkle grated paneer evenly over the dosa.
Fold the dosa in half and serve hot.

name: Sprouted Moong Poha
instructions: Rinse poha in a colander and set aside to soften.
Heat mustard oil in a pan and roast peanuts until crunchy, then remove and set aside.
In the same oil, add mustard seeds and let them splutter.
Add curry leaves and chopped green chillies, sautéing for 30 seconds.
Add lightly steamed moong sprouts, turmeric powder, and salt. Cook for 2-3 minutes.
Add the softened poha and toss gently to mix well without breaking the flakes.
Turn off the heat, stir in lemon juice and roasted peanuts.
Serve hot.

name: Moong Dal Cheela
instructions: Drain the soaked moong dal and blend it into a smooth batter with a little water.
Transfer the batter to a bowl. Mix in chopped onion, green chilli, coriander leaves, cumin, turmeric, and salt.
Heat a non-stick tawa or griddle on medium heat and brush with a little oil.
Pour a ladle of batter onto the center and spread it outwards in a circular motion to form a thin pancake.
Drizzle a little oil around the edges and cook until the base turns golden and crisp.
Flip the cheela and cook the other side for another minute.
Serve hot.

name: Sprouted Moong Chaat
instructions: In a large mixing bowl, add the lightly steamed moong sprouts.
Add finely chopped onion, tomato, green chilli, and coriander leaves.
Sprinkle red chilli powder, amchur powder, and salt over the mixture.
Pour lemon juice on top.
Toss everything well so the spices and juice coat the sprouts evenly.
Serve immediately as a fresh, high-protein meal.

name: Paneer Tikka Salad
instructions: In a bowl, mix curd, mustard oil, red chilli powder, turmeric, garam masala, salt, and lemon juice to make a marinade.
Add paneer cubes, capsicum, and onion to the marinade. Toss gently to coat and let it rest for 15 minutes.
Heat a non-stick pan on medium-high heat.
Add the marinated paneer and vegetables to the pan.
Cook for 6-8 minutes, turning occasionally until the paneer gets slightly charred edges.
Remove from heat and serve hot.

name: Rajma Rice Bowl
instructions: Pressure cook the soaked rajma with salt and enough water until soft and fully cooked.
In a separate pot, cook the basmati rice with double the amount of water until fluffy.
In a deep pan, heat oil and add cumin seeds. Let them splutter.
Add chopped onions, ginger, and garlic. Sauté until onions turn golden brown.
Add tomato purée, coriander powder, and turmeric. Cook until oil separates from the masala.
Add the boiled rajma along with its cooking water to the masala.
Simmer for 15-20 minutes on low heat to let the flavors blend and the gravy thicken.
Serve hot rajma layered over the steamed rice in a bowl.

name: Chana Masala (Dry)
instructions: Boil the soaked kabuli chana in a pressure cooker with salt and water until tender. Drain excess water.
Heat mustard oil in a heavy-bottomed pan until it starts smoking gently, then lower the heat.
Add chopped onions, ginger, and garlic, and fry until deeply golden.
Stir in tomatoes, red chilli powder, turmeric, and garam masala. Cook until the tomatoes are mushy and oil separates.
Add the boiled chana and mix well so the masala coats the chickpeas entirely.
Stir in amchur powder for tanginess and cook on low heat for 5-7 minutes until dry.
Serve hot.

name: Palak Dal
instructions: In a pressure cooker, add rinsed masoor dal, turmeric, a pinch of salt, and water. Cook until the dal is soft and mashed.
Heat oil in a pan or kadhai. Add cumin seeds and dried red chillies, and let them sizzle.
Add minced garlic and sauté until fragrant and lightly golden.
Add chopped onions and fry until translucent, then add tomatoes and cook until soft.
Add the chopped spinach and cook until wilted and completely reduced in volume.
Pour the boiled dal into the spinach mixture, adding salt to taste and a little water if needed to adjust consistency.
Simmer for 5 minutes for flavors to meld, then serve hot.

name: Goan Vegetable Xacuti
instructions: Dry roast the poppy seeds, coriander seeds, cumin, fennel, cloves, cinnamon, and dried red chillies until fragrant.
Grind the roasted spice mix with a little water to form a smooth Xacuti paste.
Heat coconut oil in a deep pan and sauté the sliced onions until soft and translucent.
Add the prepared Xacuti spice paste and turmeric powder to the pan, stirring continuously for 3 minutes.
Add the cubed potatoes and cauliflower florets to the pan, coating them well with the spice paste.
Pour in 2 cups of water, add salt, and bring the curry to a boil.
Cover the pan with a lid and simmer on medium heat for 15-20 minutes until the vegetables are cooked through.
Remove the lid and simmer for an additional 2 minutes until the gravy reaches a thick consistency.

name: Indo-Chinese Veg Fried Rice
instructions: Heat sunflower oil in a large wok or pan over high heat until smoking.
Add the minced garlic and chopped green chilli, and stir-fry quickly for 30 seconds.
Add the chopped onions and toss for 1 minute on high heat until translucent.
Add the chopped carrots, capsicum, and shredded cabbage, and stir-fry rapidly for 2-3 minutes keeping the vegetables crunchy.
Add the pre-cooked and cooled basmati rice into the wok, breaking any clumps.
Season with salt and crushed black pepper, and gently toss everything together to combine.
Stir-fry on high heat for another 2 minutes until the rice is thoroughly heated and fragrant.

name: Sindhi Kadhi
instructions: Heat oil in a deep pot and add mustard seeds, cumin seeds, fenugreek seeds, asafoetida, and curry leaves.
Once the seeds splutter, add the besan (gram flour) and roast on low flame, stirring constantly until it turns golden brown and aromatic.
Slowly pour in 4 cups of water while whisking vigorously to avoid any lumps.
Add the tomato puree, sliced onions, grated ginger, slit green chilli, turmeric powder, and red chilli powder to the pot.
Bring the mixture to a boil, then add the cubed potatoes, drumstick pieces, and salt.
Reduce the heat, cover, and let it simmer for 20-25 minutes until the vegetables are tender.
Stir in the tamarind pulp and simmer for another 5 minutes before turning off the heat.

name: Continental Veg Stir Fry
instructions: Heat sesame oil in a wide pan or skillet over medium-high heat.
Add the minced garlic and sauté for 30 seconds until fragrant without browning it.
Add the carrot batons and french beans to the pan first, as they take longer to cook, and stir-fry for 2-3 minutes.
Add the capsicum strips and shredded cabbage to the pan.
Stir-fry all the vegetables together on high heat for another 3 minutes until they are cooked but still crisp.
Season with salt and freshly cracked black pepper, tossing well to coat evenly.
Remove from heat immediately and serve hot.

name: Egg Appam

ingredients.notes: soaked and ground into a fermented batter

instructions: Heat an appam chatti (woked-pan) and lightly grease it with a few drops of coconut oil.
Pour a ladleful of fermented parboiled rice batter into the center of the pan.
Immediately swirl the pan in a circular motion so the batter spreads to form thin lacey edges and a thicker center.
Crack one whole egg directly into the center of the appam.
Sprinkle a pinch of salt and a pinch of powdered black pepper over the egg.
Cover the pan with a lid and cook on low-medium heat for about 2-3 minutes until the egg white is set and edges are crisp.
Carefully remove the appam using a spatula without breaking the center egg, and repeat for the second serving.

name: Rajma Chawal
instructions: Pressure cook soaked rajma with 4 cups water and 1 tsp salt for 6–7 whistles until soft. Reserve the cooking liquid.
Cook soaked basmati rice in 400ml water with a pinch of salt until fully cooked, then fluff with a fork and set aside.
Heat ghee in a heavy-bottomed pan over medium heat. Add cumin seeds and let them splutter for 30 seconds.
Add chopped onion and sauté for 8–10 minutes until deep golden brown.
Add ginger and garlic paste and cook for 2 minutes until the raw aroma disappears.
Pour in tomato purée, add turmeric, red chilli powder, and coriander powder. Cook for 6–8 minutes until oil separates.
Add cooked rajma along with 1 cup reserved cooking liquid. Stir to combine.
Simmer on low heat for 12–15 minutes, mashing a few rajma lightly to thicken the gravy.
Stir in garam masala. Adjust salt and simmer for 2 more minutes.
Garnish with chopped coriander leaves. Serve hot rajma over steamed basmati rice.

name: Chole Bhature

ingredients.notes: absorbed during frying bhaturas (use more for bath, drain on towels)

instructions: Knead maida with curd, a pinch of salt, and enough water to form a soft smooth dough. Cover and rest for 2 hours.
Pressure cook soaked kabuli chana with bay leaf, cinnamon, cloves, and salt for 5–6 whistles until tender. Reserve cooking liquid.
Heat ghee in a kadai. Add cumin and let it splutter, then add chopped onion and sauté until golden brown, about 8 minutes.
Add ginger, garlic, and green chilli; cook 2 minutes. Add tomato purée, turmeric, red chilli powder, and cook until oil separates.
Add cooked chana with 1 cup cooking liquid. Stir and simmer 15 minutes until gravy thickens.
Add amchur powder and garam masala. Adjust salt and simmer 3 more minutes. Garnish with coriander.
Divide the rested bhatura dough into 4 equal balls and roll each into an oval about 5mm thick.
Heat oil in a deep pan to 180°C. Fry each bhatura one at a time, pressing gently with a ladle so it puffs, about 1–2 minutes per side.
Drain bhaturas on paper towels. Serve hot with chole and sliced onion on the side.

name: Dal Chawal Tadka
instructions: Pressure cook toor dal with 2.5 cups water, turmeric, and a pinch of salt for 4–5 whistles until mushy. Whisk smooth.
Cook soaked basmati rice separately with 320ml water until grains are cooked and separate. Fluff and set aside.
Heat 20g ghee in a pan. Add cumin seeds and asafoetida; let splutter for 30 seconds.
Add onion and sauté on medium heat for 7–8 minutes until light golden.
Add garlic and ginger, cook 2 minutes. Add tomato and cook until soft and oil separates.
Add red chilli powder and cooked dal. Stir well, add water to adjust consistency, and simmer 8 minutes.
Add garam masala and lemon juice. Stir and simmer 2 more minutes.
For the final tadka, heat remaining 10g ghee in a small pan, add dried red chillies and a pinch of cumin; pour over dal.
Garnish with coriander leaves and serve hot dal over steamed basmati rice.

name: Paneer Butter Masala with Naan
instructions: Mix maida with curd, a pinch of salt, and enough warm water to form a soft pliable dough. Rest covered for 30 minutes.
Blend tomato, garlic, ginger, green cardamom, cloves, and bay leaf with a splash of water into a smooth tomato puree. Strain for a silkier texture if desired.
Heat 20g butter in a pan. Cook the blended purée over medium heat for 10–12 minutes until it thickens and butter floats on top.
Add red chilli powder, turmeric, and cashew paste. Stir and cook 3 minutes.
Add paneer cubes, salt, and sugar. Gently stir and cook 5 minutes.
Stir in fresh cream, garam masala, and crushed kasuri methi. Simmer on low heat 3 minutes. Garnish with coriander.
Divide naan dough into 4 portions. Roll each into an oval about 4mm thick.
Heat a tawa or flat pan until very hot. Place naan and cook 1–2 minutes until bubbles form, then flip and cook the other side.
Brush each naan with remaining butter as it comes off the heat. Serve hot naans alongside the paneer butter masala.

name: Aloo Paratha Thali
instructions: Knead whole wheat flour with water and a pinch of salt into a soft smooth dough. Cover and rest for 20 minutes.
Mix mashed potato with onion, green chilli, ginger, coriander, cumin, red chilli powder, amchur, garam masala, and salt to form the filling.
For the raita, whisk curd with grated carrot, black salt, and a pinch of cumin. Chill until serving.
Divide dough into 4 equal balls. Flatten each ball, place a generous portion of potato filling in the centre, and seal the edges.
Gently roll each stuffed ball into a round paratha about 5–6mm thick, taking care not to tear the dough.
Heat a tawa over medium-high heat. Place a paratha on the tawa and cook for 1–2 minutes until bubbles appear on the surface.
Flip the paratha, spread about 5g ghee on the cooked side, and cook the other side for 1–2 minutes.
Flip again, apply ghee on the second side, and press gently with a spatula for even browning. Cook until golden spots appear.
Repeat for all 4 parathas. Serve 2 hot parathas per person with chilled curd raita on the side.

name: Veg Biryani
instructions: Par-boil soaked basmati rice in salted boiling water with bay leaf, cardamom, and cinnamon until 70% cooked. Drain and set aside.
Heat ghee in a heavy pot. Add whole spices (cardamom, cloves, star anise, cinnamon) and sauté 30 seconds.
Add sliced onion and fry on medium heat for 10–12 minutes until deep golden brown. Remove half the onion and set aside for garnish.
Add ginger-garlic paste and green chilli; cook 2 minutes. Add tomato, turmeric, red chilli powder, and cook until oil separates.
Add all vegetables and curd. Stir well, season with salt, and cook on medium heat for 8 minutes.
Spread the par-cooked rice evenly over the vegetable layer. Drizzle saffron milk and garam masala on top.
Scatter reserved fried onion and coriander leaves over the rice. Cover the pot tightly with a lid or foil.
Cook on the lowest flame (or on a tawa as a heat diffuser) for 20–25 minutes for the dum.
Open the lid gently, mix lightly from the edges, and serve hot biryani with curd raita.

name: Vegan Rajma Rice Bowl
instructions: Pressure cook soaked rajma with 4 cups water and salt for 6–7 whistles until very soft. Reserve the cooking liquid.
Cook soaked sona masoori rice with 400ml water until fully cooked, then fluff and set aside.
Heat sunflower oil in a heavy pan over medium heat. Add cumin seeds and let them splutter.
Add chopped onion and fry for 8–10 minutes until deep golden brown.
Add ginger and garlic; cook 2 minutes. Add tomato purée and cook until oil separates, about 6 minutes.
Add coriander powder, turmeric, and red chilli powder. Cook the masala for 2 more minutes.
Add cooked rajma with 1 cup reserved liquid. Mash a few rajma to thicken the curry.
Simmer on low heat for 12–15 minutes. Add garam masala. Adjust salt.
Serve the rajma curry generously over bowls of steamed sona masoori rice, garnished with coriander.

name: Chana Masala with Rice
instructions: Pressure cook soaked kabuli chana with bay leaf, a pinch of salt, and 4 cups water for 5–6 whistles. Reserve the cooking liquid.
Cook soaked basmati rice in 400ml salted water until fully cooked. Fluff with a fork and set aside.
Heat sunflower oil in a kadai. Add cumin seeds; let them splutter, then add green chilli.
Add onion and sauté on medium heat for 8–10 minutes until deep brown.
Add ginger and garlic, cook 2 minutes. Pour in tomato purée; cook for 7–8 minutes until oil separates.
Add coriander powder, turmeric, and red chilli powder. Stir and cook the masala 2 minutes.
Add cooked chana and 1.5 cups cooking liquid. Mix well and bring to a boil.
Simmer for 15 minutes, mashing a few chickpeas to thicken. Add garam masala, amchur, and lemon juice.
Simmer 3 more minutes, adjust salt, and garnish with coriander. Serve hot over steamed basmati rice.

name: Bisi Bele Bath (Full Portion)
name_alt: Karnataka Spiced Rice and Lentil One-Pot
instructions: Pressure cook toor dal with 1.5 cups water and turmeric for 4 whistles until soft. Mash and set aside.
In the same or another pressure cooker, cook rice with 2 cups water for 3 whistles until soft and slightly mushy.
In a large heavy pot, heat groundnut oil. Add mustard seeds and let them pop.
Add dried red chillies, curry leaves, and asafoetida. Sauté 30 seconds.
Add onion and sauté until translucent. Add tomato and cook until soft.
Add carrot, french beans, and green peas. Stir-fry for 3–4 minutes.
Add tamarind water, red chilli powder, coriander powder, and salt. Simmer 5 minutes.
Add cooked rice and dal to the pot. Stir everything together over low heat.
Add jaggery and roasted peanuts. Mix well and cook for another 10 minutes, adding water if needed to reach a porridge-like consistency.
Garnish with coriander leaves and serve hot in bowls.

name: Egg Biryani (Full Plate)
instructions: Hard boil all 6 eggs for 10 minutes, cool, peel, and make 3–4 shallow cuts on each egg. Rub with a little turmeric and red chilli powder.
Par-boil soaked basmati rice in salted boiling water with whole spices (bay leaf, cardamom, cinnamon, cloves, star anise) until 70% cooked. Drain.
Heat 20g ghee in a heavy pot. Fry the spiced eggs for 2–3 minutes until lightly golden. Remove and set aside.
In the same pot, add sliced onion and fry in the remaining ghee for 10–12 minutes until deep golden. Remove half for garnish.
Add ginger-garlic paste and green chilli; cook 2 minutes. Add tomato and cook until soft.
Add red chilli powder, curd, and salt. Mix well and cook 5 minutes until masala thickens.
Place fried eggs back into the masala and coat well.
Layer the par-cooked rice over the egg masala. Drizzle saffron water and garam masala over the rice.
Top with reserved fried onion and coriander leaves. Seal with lid and cook on the lowest flame for 20 minutes for dum.
Open gently, mix from the edges, and serve hot. Plate 3 eggs and rice per person.

name: Egg Paratha Thali
instructions: Knead whole wheat flour with water and a pinch of salt into a soft, smooth dough. Cover and rest for 20 minutes.
Whisk eggs with onion, tomato, green chilli, coriander, red chilli powder, turmeric, garam masala, and salt to make the egg filling mixture.
For the raita, whisk curd with a pinch of cumin, black salt, and chopped coriander. Chill until serving.
Divide the dough into 4 equal balls. Roll each into a medium-thin round.
Heat a tawa over medium-high heat. Place a paratha and cook for 1 minute until the top surface starts drying.
Pour 1/4 of the egg mixture over the paratha, spreading it evenly. Flip quickly so the egg side is on the tawa.
Apply 5g ghee around the edges and on top. Cook for 1–2 minutes until the egg is set and golden.
Flip once more, press gently with the spatula, and cook for 30 seconds. Remove from heat.
Repeat for all 4 parathas. Serve 2 egg parathas per person with chilled curd raita on the side.

name: Chicken Biryani (Full Plate)
instructions: Marinate chicken thigh pieces with curd, ginger-garlic paste, red chilli powder, turmeric, garam masala, salt, and lemon juice for at least 1 hour.
Par-boil soaked basmati rice in salted boiling water with whole spices (bay leaf, cardamom, cinnamon, cloves, star anise, fennel) until 70% cooked. Drain.
Heat 25g ghee in a heavy pot. Fry sliced onion for 12–15 minutes until very dark golden and crispy. Remove half for garnish.
In the remaining ghee and onion, add the marinated chicken. Sear on high heat for 3–4 minutes on each side.
Add chopped tomato and green chilli. Stir, cover, and cook on medium heat for 20 minutes until chicken is cooked through and masala thickens.
Layer the par-cooked rice over the chicken masala evenly.
Drizzle saffron water and remaining 15g ghee over the rice. Top with reserved fried onion and coriander leaves.
Seal the pot tightly with a lid or foil. Cook on the lowest flame (or place on a tawa) for 25 minutes.
Open gently and mix from the bottom and sides. Check chicken is fully cooked.
Serve hot, plating chicken pieces with fragrant rice per person.

name: Mutton Pulao
instructions: Heat ghee in a pressure cooker. Add all whole spices (bay leaf, cinnamon, cloves, both cardamoms, star anise, mace, fennel) and sauté 30 seconds.
Add sliced onion and fry on medium heat for 10–12 minutes until golden brown.
Add ginger-garlic paste and green chilli; cook 2 minutes until the raw smell is gone.
Add mutton pieces and sear on high heat for 4–5 minutes until browned on all sides.
Add curd, red chilli powder, turmeric, and salt. Mix well. Add 1 cup water, close the pressure cooker and cook for 4–5 whistles until mutton is 80% done.
Open when pressure releases. Check the mutton gravy — it should be thick and fragrant.
Add soaked and drained basmati rice to the mutton and its stock. Add hot water so the total liquid is 1.5x the volume of rice.
Adjust salt. Bring to a boil uncovered, then lower heat, cover, and cook for 12–15 minutes until rice is fully cooked and liquid is absorbed.
Sprinkle garam masala and fluff the pulao gently with a fork. Rest covered for 5 minutes.
Garnish with coriander leaves and serve hot, plating mutton pieces with rice per person.

name: Butter Chicken with Rice
instructions: Marinate chicken breast cubes with curd, half the red chilli powder, turmeric, and salt for at least 30 minutes.
Cook soaked basmati rice in 400ml salted water until fully cooked. Fluff with a fork and set aside.
Grill or pan-fry marinated chicken in a non-stick pan over high heat for 6–8 minutes until charred spots appear. Set aside.
In the same pan, heat 20g butter. Sauté onion, garlic, ginger, cardamom, cloves, and cinnamon until onion is soft.
Add tomato purée, remaining red chilli powder, and cook for 10–12 minutes until the masala thickens and butter separates.
Cool the mixture slightly, then blend smooth. Pass through a strainer for a silky sauce.
Return the sauce to the pan over medium heat. Add remaining 20g butter and stir in.
Add grilled chicken pieces to the sauce. Simmer 10 minutes.
Stir in fresh cream, sugar, garam masala, and crushed kasuri methi. Simmer 3 minutes. Adjust salt.
Garnish with coriander and a swirl of cream. Serve butter chicken over steamed basmati rice.

name: Fish Curry with Rice
instructions: Marinate rohu fish pieces with 1/2 tsp turmeric, salt, and lemon juice for 15 minutes.
Cook sona masoori rice in 400ml salted water until fully cooked. Fluff and set aside.
Heat mustard oil in a kadai until it reaches smoking point, then lower the flame to let it cool slightly. This removes pungency.
Shallow-fry the marinated fish pieces for 2–3 minutes per side until golden. Remove and set aside.
In the same oil, add mustard seeds and bay leaf; let them splutter. Add cumin and sauté 20 seconds.
Add sliced onion and cook for 6–7 minutes until golden. Add ginger-garlic paste and cook 2 minutes.
Add tomato, remaining turmeric, red chilli powder, and coriander powder. Cook until oil separates.
Add potato cubes and 2 cups water. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 10 minutes until potatoes are half cooked.
Gently slide in the fried fish pieces and green chillies. Simmer on low heat for 8–10 minutes. Adjust salt.
Garnish with coriander leaves and serve the fish curry alongside steamed sona masoori rice.
